hearthstead.guide.attributes.body: Every settler has eight numeric attributes, each shown from 0 to 100: Strength for heavy work and carrying; Stamina for keeping pace while tired; Wits for learning; Dexterity for precise hands; Spirit for morale under pressure; Perception for finding targets; Focus for staying on task; and Presence for leading and reassuring others. Newcomers begin low, except for one natural knack that leans higher. The numbers make people different; they never choose the worker for you.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.body2: Attributes grow only by doing the work that trains them — a lumberer's axe builds Strength, a courier's rounds build Stamina. Growth is slow and never finishes: a settler trained for weeks is one you built. Wits speeds every attribute's growth, itself included, so schooling a clever settler early pays for life. Most settlers carry a trait, sometimes two, and every trait costs something: strong backs carry more and walk slower; quick studies learn faster, a step behind on everything else.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.title: Attributes
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.body: Workers have Energy and a visible Work Pace, not a hidden daily-work quota. As Energy falls, they keep accepting valid work but move and complete it more slowly. They do not abruptly stop for the rest of the day because an invisible allowance reached zero. Check the settler sheet to see both Energy and the current pace.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.body2: Rest and the normal daily routine restore Energy. Stamina determines how much pace a tired worker keeps: stronger Stamina means a higher minimum pace when Energy is low. A tired worker may be much slower, but a valid task remains valid; equipment, route and workplace blockers are reported separately.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.title: Work Pace
hearthstead.guide.day.body:
The whole settlement shares one clock. At Rise everyone wakes and the square fills; through Morning and Afternoon Work they walk to their trade — unless it is farmed or felled, where the work already is. At the midday Meal they gather in the dining hall, and come Evening the tavern and square fill again before Rest sends everyone to bed. A phase is a habit, never a law: a raid or real exhaustion overrides it. Guards keep half their number on a night watch, so someone is always walking.

TAVERN TABLES
Hire an Innkeeper by buying their Job Emblem from the Guildmaster, holding it and right-clicking the intended settler. Keep ready-to-eat food and at least one glass bottle together in one chest or barrel inside the Tavern; the bottle is reusable. Wheat is an ingredient: craft vanilla bread before it becomes a meal. Edible carrots and beetroots can stock the Banner's stores when a Courier carries them from linked Warehouse storage; a Tavern needs ready food and reusable bottles in its own service store. Keep spare meals and glass bottles in linked Warehouse storage. A Courier refills a staffed Tavern after the Banner has its food reserve. Place an Another Furniture wooden chair facing an adjacent wooden table. Keep the chair pulled out. You can also use a bottom-half straight stair with its low side facing a fence topped by a wooden pressure plate. Leave a clear side aisle beside the chair and space across the table for the host to stand. Keep the furniture and both approach spaces inside the linked Tavern. Residents visit during Meal and Evening when free from work and urgent needs. Guards keep their watch and orders.
hearthstead.guide.day.title: The Day
hearthstead.guide.founding.body:
Craft a Banner (3 logs, 5 cobblestone and a campfire) and place it on open ground away from other settlements, with two free blocks above it. Four founding workers arrive, and the Guildmaster takes his stool beside the Banner. The four founders can rest by the Banner until homes exist; every settler you recruit later needs a free bed. Right-click the Banner and press Journey: it always shows your next step. Your town's claim reaches 72 blocks from the Banner (server option [settlement] radius): raiders form up just outside it, and a second Banner must stand at least twice that far away.

FIRST STEPS
After you raise your banner the Guildmaster welcomes you with 4 Coins for the treasury, and iron tools and 16 bread for each player. Trade logs, iron or crops with the Traveling Merchant who comes to the Banner (see Coins & the Merchant). Mine copper and iron early: every building needs a Plaque (5 copper, 1 iron, 3 planks). In Banner → Tech Tree, learn Lumber Camp (1 Coin, 8 logs, 8 cobblestone). Build and register the camp, then right-click the Guildmaster beside the Banner and buy a Lumberer Emblem (1 Coin, 2 flint). Use it on a founder, mark trees with the Work Scepter and put any axe in the camp chest. The first stored logs open Stores & Roads.

Coins and goods are physical items. Purchases take them from your inventory first, then the settlement's Banner, then linked Warehouse storage. If a purchase is refused, the message lists exactly what is missing.
hearthstead.guide.founding.title: Founding
hearthstead.guide.jobs.body:
Jobs are authorised by physical Job Emblems. Learn and register the workplace, then buy its Emblem from the Guildmaster at the Banner. Hold it in your main hand and right-click a compatible settler without sneaking: Bannerhold consumes it once and automatically assigns the nearest valid workplace. There is no separate Hire button. Every new worker starts with no job equipment; their need icon, inventory and the open requests on Banner → Storage show the real item they need. Rejected assignments do not consume the Emblem. Empty both hands and Shift-right-click a settler when you want to open their inventory yourself.

The Hunter shoots one wild animal at a time within 28 blocks of his Lodge, never below five of a species and never inside your pens. He carries the carcass home on his shoulders, butchers it (fast on a Butchering Table: flint, 3 wooden slabs, 2 logs) and stores the meat and hides in the Lodge chest for the Courier. While he works there, wild game slowly returns to the open land around the Lodge.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.title: Jobs
hearthstead.guide.logistics.body:
Workers collect and deliver physical goods using their bags and workplace storage. Plan about one Courier for every 10 settlers: every meal reaches the Banner from Warehouse storage in a Courier's bag, and workshops are restocked the same way. A crafter whose workshop runs empty fetches its own materials from a nearby Warehouse when no Courier is free, and tidies the workshop, sharpens tools and studies the trade while there is truly nothing to make. Open Banner → Storage to see the open requests and deliveries: each row names the goods, and hovering it shows the route, the assigned Courier and any Stop reason. Real stacks move from the workplace chest through the Courier bag into Warehouse storage. Equipment follows a real request from storage to the worker. A blocked route or missing tool stays visible until its cause is resolved.

Open Banner → Storage → Stores to find goods and inspect the loaded Warehouse locations that hold them. This is a stock overview; open the real chest to take items. An unloaded Warehouse is not reported as an empty one.

Worker-made goods can have better quality than ordinary goods. Timber, iron and honey cost 8 / 7 / 6 / 5 / 4 / 4 items per Coin from Basic through Legendary; field goods cost 16 / 14 / 12 / 10 / 9 / 8. Basic, Fine and Superior offers hold up to four Coin sales, Exceptional and Masterwork two, and Legendary one. The visitor's shared purse is the total market limit: 12 Coins, plus 2 for every 5 settlers, at most 40. He also buys three kinds of crafted goods each visit, such as bread, cooked meat, leather, stone bricks, charcoal, wool, beams and iron tools, chosen from what your village holds. Moving goods through a bag or chest does not improve quality. Check the exact offer before trading.

Bigger loads: the Courier Satchel, Leather Pack and Frame Pack grow every Courier's sack (+50 / +100 / +150%), and Worker Packs let Lumberers and Farmers use the same sack. The Hand Cart adds +200% more: the Courier pulls it along roads, parks it outside and carries the last steps by hand. Carts are quick on roads and slow on grass, so lay dirt paths or gravel from the Warehouse to your workplaces. Paved Roads makes everyone 15% faster on those roads.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.title: Logistics
hearthstead.guide.plaque.body: A hung plaque starts blank and does nothing at all — no screen, no scan — until you fit a Build Plan into it. Craft a plan for the building you want and use it on the plaque: that stamps its purpose and sets it surveying the room around it. The plaque glows what it finds: dark while blank, red until something is met, amber once part of the room qualifies, green the moment all of it does.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.body2:
Each building has its own requirements for floor space, furniture, storage and access. Right-click its plaque for the exact checklist. Green checks show fulfilled requirements; missing entries explain what to build. The room is checked again automatically; Refresh requests a new reading.

After Timber Rights, craft a Work Scepter from 2 flint, 1 copper ingot and 2 sticks. Hold it and right-click a Lumber Camp, Farmhouse or the employed worker. Right-click each corner, then right-click the height. Review and confirm the outlined work area. Trees and crops must be inside that area.

A building may be placed beyond the Banner's central area when it is linked to the settlement. Keep entrances and routes usable. Beds show their status on the sheet: yellow = free, green = taken, red = not in a valid room.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.title: The Plaque
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.body:
Travelers set out for your settlement during ordinary play once it has a bound Banner, a valid Tavern, a free bed, enough morale and a food reserve. When one is waiting, open the Banner, choose People, then Traveler to see their card, and press Recruit Traveler. New guests ask 4 to 8 Coins: a stronger start costs more, and an Innkeeper or Dining Hall lowers the price. The card keeps the exact price, which is charged only if recruitment succeeds. You can earn Coins while the guest waits.

Recruitment needs a free bed and a ready-meal reserve at the Banner. Before the first raid ends this reserve is capped at 16 by default; later it is 8 per resident, counting the newcomer. A House counts at most 4 beds (6 once you learn Townhouses, 8 with Manors); extra beds in a full House stay empty, while a Lodging counts all its beds. Coins can come from your inventory, the settlement's Banner and linked Warehouse containers.

A waiting traveler may sit in a staffed Tavern. Visiting guests with Coins pay one Coin for a meal, and the Coin goes into settlement storage. Residents use the normal meal service. Sitting and buying a meal do not make a visitor a resident, and recruiting never skips the bed check.
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.title: Recruiting
hearthstead.guide.research.body: Research needs a built and registered Architect's Study. First complete the first-raid aftermath. Then learn Commons Doctrine in the Banner's Tech Tree: keep every resident housed for 20 continuous minutes, fulfil 5 equipment requests, and pay 6 Coins, 4 books and 8 bread. The first doctrine you learn stays the settlement's primary tradition; you can still earn the other released doctrines later at full cost. Build the study with its learned plan, then right-click its lectern to open the research bench. Hire a Scholar to advance projects. An employed Scholar also adds a little progress each day when not working at the lectern. Each project costs paper and a trade sample. Cancelling returns half the sample, never the paper.
hearthstead.guide.research.body2: The catalogue lists six projects, and all of them can be started. Better Yeast, Bellows Smelting and Tannic Acid speed up the Baker, Smelter and Tanner, whose trades open with Land and Harvest and Craft and Industry. Seasoned timber may be researched before unlocking or building a sawmill; its bonus helps only when a sawyer produces there. Choose one project at a time and pay its displayed physical cost. Completed research gives a permanent bonus. Existing paid projects can still progress or be cancelled. Research is optional.
hearthstead.guide.research.title: Research
hearthstead.guide.saga.body: Every raid captain who reaches your walls has a name, and one who gets away with what they came for earns a second — 'the Grain-Thief' for one who stole your harvest, 'Larder's Bane' for one who has done it more than once — each a claim you can check against the raid's own report. A captain remembers too: the settler who hurt them most becomes a grudge carried into the next fight, and cutting one down only passes it on — whoever answers next inherits both the grudge and a name sworn to the one who fell.
hearthstead.guide.saga.title: The Saga
hearthstead.guide.coins.title: Coins & the Merchant
hearthstead.guide.coins.body: Coins are physical items and the settlement's only currency. The first Traveling Merchant sets out soon after founding when a route is available; later visits need a player within 80 blocks and keep their normal 20-minute cadence. Right-click the merchant and trade the goods it wants. Basic logs, iron and fish sell at 8 per Coin, and crops at 16. Higher-quality goods need fewer items. Each merchant's shared purse holds 12 Coins. Each offer can be used four times, and repeat sales of one kind of goods cost 25% more, so bring a mix.
hearthstead.guide.coins.body2: Later income: winning the first raid pays 8 Coins into the Banner's stores, and each later victory pays 4. A Trader at a Trading Post sells settlement goods for you. You spend Coins on Tech Tree knowledge and upgrades, and on Job Emblems plus goods (Lumberer 1 Coin, most jobs 2, Guard and Archer 3). Recruits cost 4 to 8 Coins. Payments take from your inventory first, then the Banner, then linked Warehouse chests. The Tech Tree shows the Coins available, and a refused purchase lists what is missing.
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.title: Work Zones
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.body: Lumberers and Farmers only work inside a Work Zone you draw. After learning Lumber Camp, craft a Work Scepter from 2 flint, 1 copper ingot and 2 sticks. Hold it and right-click the Lumber Camp or Farmhouse plaque, or its employed worker. Right-click the first ground corner, then the opposite corner, then once more at the height you want. Review the outlined 3D box and press Confirm Zone; Cancel changes nothing. A worker's settler sheet also offers Edit Work Zone.
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.body2: A Lumber Zone must contain a natural tree with its trunk and leaves. A Farm Zone must contain farmland or a planted crop, plus at least one block of growing space above. Zones can be anywhere, even outside the settlement, as long as they are in loaded chunks; keep them near your storage so workers do not walk far. A zone can be at most 48 x 64 x 48 blocks. A Farmer's field starts at 12 x 12 and grows by 4 blocks for every 20 Dexterity, up to 28 x 28. A worker without a zone shows NO WORK ZONE in the open requests on Banner → Storage.
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.title: Tech Tree
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.body: Open the Banner and choose Tech Tree. The Banner sits in the middle; ranks are rings (Hamlet inside, then Village, Town, Castle) and each branch owns a wedge: Watch, Logistics, Commons and Craft. When the tree opens, the node your Journey asks for next is selected and wears a gold Journey ribbon: for a new village that is Timber Rights (Lumber Camp). Click a node to see its cost, milestones and what it unlocks. Research asks twice: the first click shows "Confirm" with the full price, the second click pays (hold Shift to skip the confirm). A red line warns you when a purchase would spend the Coin your Journey step needs. Coins and goods are paid once, from your pack, the Banner and the Warehouse.
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.body2: Charters are wax seals on the top spoke: surviving the first raid stamps the Village Charter, and the Town and Castle Charters open the outer rings (they take in-game days of study). A dashed red pair is a pick-one: learning one closes the other for good. Some nodes are marked Planned: they are not in the game yet and cannot be learned. Items and building plans are only craftable once their node is learned; a padlocked result tells you which node you need. Scroll out for the whole map, in for names and costs; the filter chips turn one branch to the top and the rank ladder at the bottom zooms to a ring.
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.title: Trade Levels
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.body: Every settler has a level from 1 to 10 in each trade they practise. Each real piece of work, such as a felled tree, a harvest or a delivery, earns trade XP, about 25 a day. Level 2 needs 25 XP, and level 10 takes about 44 days of steady work. A settler who changes jobs starts the new trade at level 1 but keeps the XP of the old one. Guards and Archers earn combat ranks instead (see The Watch). The settler sheet shows the level, the XP to the next level and the current bonuses.
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.body2:
Each trade has a primary and a secondary attribute:
Lumberer and Courier: Strength, then Stamina
Farmer: Dexterity, then Stamina
Fisher: Dexterity, then Perception
Hunter: Perception, then Dexterity
Innkeeper: Presence, then Spirit
Trader: Wits, then Presence
Scholar: Wits, then Focus
Each level above 1 makes the worker up to 2% faster, depending on the primary attribute, to a maximum of 18%. From level 5 the secondary attribute adds a side bonus of up to 8%. Work trains the primary attribute at full rate and the secondary at half. Wits, the settler's intelligence, speeds up all trade XP by up to 25%.
hearthstead.guide.crafting_orders.title: Crafting Orders
hearthstead.guide.crafting_orders.body: When a workplace runs short of materials, fuel or Tavern stock, it opens a crafting order by itself; you never create one. The order first looks in the workplace's own storage, then in the Warehouse, then asks a staffed workshop that can make the item. When no workshop can make it, the order is marked Needs you and listed near the top of the open requests on Banner → Storage. Put the item into that workplace's storage or a Warehouse chest, and the order closes on its own. A worker who needs a tool gets it the same way: the Smithy forges it, and if there is no iron for a pickaxe it forges a stone one from cobblestone. Orders never stop anyone from working; they only tell crafters what to make first.
hearthstead.guide.tavern.title: Tavern Evenings
hearthstead.guide.tavern.body: Learn Tavern & Inn, then build a Tavern with a bell, 2 chests or barrels, an Ale Tap, a door, 3 lights and 36 floor blocks. The bell can be made with gold or copper ingots. Right-click the Tavern's plaque for its live checklist. You need a Tavern to recruit travelers and to be ready for the first raid. Hire an Innkeeper (2 Coins, 2 bread, 2 leather). The Innkeeper brews ale from wheat at the Ale Tap and serves meals from the Tavern's store. You can buy ale at the tap for 1 Coin and an empty bottle.
hearthstead.guide.tavern.body2: In the evening, free residents walk to the Tavern and take a seat. A seat is a wooden chair facing a table, or a stair facing a fence topped by a wooden pressure plate. One seated resident plays as the bard; it is never a Guard, an Archer or the Innkeeper. Guests who finish a Tavern meal or ale while the bard plays gain +5 morale, once a day. A table service takes a ready meal and an empty bottle from the same Tavern chest or barrel; a Courier refills it from the Banner. When it runs dry, seated guests show "No food at the Tavern" and leave when their visit ends. The music stops during an alarm or when a raid is due. Visiting travelers pay 1 Coin for a meal.
hearthstead.guide.raids.title: Raids & the Alarm Bell
hearthstead.guide.raids.body: The first raid never comes by surprise. It is set on a timer, about three days after founding, even before you have guards; choosing Declare Ready in Journey also sets it for a later night. One dusk before every raid, a warning names the night, captain, direction and objective. After each raid the next one is set 3 to 4 days later. Missed nights are not replayed. Raids grow with the settlement: the first raids are small bands of outlaws, skirmishers join from the second, and Brutes only come from the fourth raid, and only when you have three or more fighters. The band is sized to your Guards, Archers and their weapons, so losing defenders also makes the next band smaller. The Banner screen shows the next planned night or the recovery time left. Each victory pays Coins into the Banner's stores: 8 for the first, then 4.
hearthstead.guide.raids.body2: Any vanilla bell inside the settlement is an alarm bell, including the Tavern's. Right-click it, or hit it with an arrow, to sound two minutes of alarm; ring again to extend it. Civilians run to their homes, and Guards and Archers without orders head for the bell. Defenders with a post or patrol keep it. When a raid is announced or arrives, a living Guard or Archer rings the bell you last used, or one near the Banner. The all-clear sounds when the raid ends. You cannot sleep while raiders are in the settlement.
hearthstead.guide.summons.body: Right-click a working building's plaque and press Summon to call whoever works there straight to their post — useful for a farmer sleeping off a bad night in the wrong field, or a guard who wandered off to watch instead of fight. A bell rings where you stood; the settler answers with a low murmur wherever they are, then starts walking, glowing the whole way through walls so you can watch them coming. A summons lasts about a minute and a half — past that they simply forget they were called, and the glow fades with it.
hearthstead.guide.summons.title: Summons
hearthstead.guide.threat.body: The first raid approaches on a timer, about three days after founding by default. A warning one dusk beforehand names its night, captain and band. It can arrive before you have guards or a Barracks. An undefended village faces a small band of weak raiders; armed Guards and Archers increase its size, up to six. Prepare weapons, meals and clear routes, and fight beside your settlers. The raid retreats at dawn and also has a finite time limit. Journey still offers its preparation checklist and the existing Declare Ready route; unfinished checklist steps do not stop the automatic timer.
hearthstead.guide.threat.body2: After the raid, check the outcome and losses, replace missing equipment and restock the Banner food. First Raid Aftermath in the Tech Tree opens upgrades and doctrines once its requirements are met. The first victory pays 8 Coins. Later raids return on a schedule, so keep your defenders supplied. A timer raid does not automatically complete unfinished Journey preparation steps.

hearthstead.guide.title: Settler's Handbook
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.s: Story Visitors
Named visitors come for real milestones and remember every visit. Talk to them for gifts, news and blessings; upset one and they will remember it.
Warnings and Threats
A warlord's herald or a lord's bailiff warns you off, then warns again. Pay, talk them down or defy them; defy the warlord twice and he leads your next raid.
The Hollins (neighbours)
The farm family over the ridge brings a basket of food and seed. Thank them, or give food back; they return as the village grows.
Pell Rook (herald)
The neighbour lord's herald brings a letter when your rank rises. The gift follows your standing with that lord; tearing it up angers him.
Odo Farthing (merchant)
A merchant who remembers your custom and counts his visits. Thank him for a free rare ware, or buy him a drink.
A settler's thanks
One of your own settlers thanks you at a milestone. They walk up to you with a small gift from their trade.
Wenna Lark (bard)
After a held raid she sings of the captain you beat. Listen or tip her; everyone's mood lifts.
The Brisks (newcomers)
A family drawn by your fame asks to join; needs 3 free beds. Take them in, feed them, or turn them away (they will remember).
Brother Anselm (pilgrim)
A pilgrim blesses your Banner and wishes you luck. Accept for a Luck blessing; a donation makes it longer.
Mother Gerd (healer)
After a raid that hurt settlers, she heals the wounded. Let her heal everyone and take her healing draughts.
Sergeant Brannoc (old soldier)
An old soldier inspects your guards. Let him drill them for morale; the first time he gives you a shield.
Old Hilde (storyteller)
She tells your own village's story at the Tavern. Listen or tip her for morale.
Sigrun Crowvoice (Varg's herald)
"You cannot stay here." Then: "Last warning." Two enforcers come. Pay tribute, talk, or defy; defied twice, Varg Ironjaw leads your next raid.
Reeve Hamon Stark (bailiff)
If you anger the neighbour lord, his bailiff demands a land tax. Pay, make amends with food, or defy him and fight his men-at-arms.
Gorm Stonebelly (brute chief)
The brute toll's chief remembers how the last toll ended. Kill his band and he comes back with a fourth brute.
hearthstead.guide.tech_branches.founding: The five trades round the Banner: Lumber Camp, Fishery, Fields, Hunters' Lodge and Trading Post.
Each needs only the Banner (the Lumber Camp also 3 settlers) and costs 1-3 Coins: wood, food, hides and Coins on day one.
Open the Banner, then Tech Tree: they are the inner ring.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.trad: Build a Trading Post; a Trader sells your surplus for Coins.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.b: Early raids are outlaw bands led by a bandit leader. Like a raid captain he halts to talk first: pay him off in coin or food, talk him into moving on, warn him off if your town has real guards or towers, fight him alone, or refuse. Paid or persuaded bands walk away; they never vanish in front of you.
A bare barter screen opened directly on an NPC with trade stock. Pick goods on both sides and accept the deal, or leave.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.d: A test peddler conversation for admins. Only spawned by the admin command /hstalk peddler; not part of normal play.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.r: Before a recurring raid charges, its captain halts at the edge and waits to talk. Pay tribute, persuade a truce, duel the captain alone, or refuse and fight.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.t: A data-driven sample talk: a traveller trades news for bread. Only spawned by the admin command /hstalk traveller; not part of normal play.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.livingvill: Settler life around the village: chatter, idle visits and small daily habits.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.weapons.te: Damage, speed and reach of the captain weapons per type and tier.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.hud.name: [hud]
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.hud.text: healthCounter: a small heart and HP at the top of the screen for whoever you look at (top, the default) or off. It turns gold only when that enemy can be finished.
hearthstead.guide.jobs_directory.list1.b: Every job in Bannerhold: what it does, how you hire it and where it works.
hearthstead.guide.jobs_directory.list1.t: Buy an Emblem from the Guildmaster, then give it to a settler.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.non: An unassigned settler waiting for a job. Hire: Every new settler starts unassigned. Firing a worker returns them here.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.far: Tills, sows and harvests the fields you mark, then stores the wheat. Hire: Buy the Farmer Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 8 Wheat Seeds, 1 Leather). Works at: Farmhouse.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.lum: Fells trees in its work area and hauls the logs to camp; with Sharpened Axes, whets the axe every 8 trees. Hire: Buy the Lumberer Emblem from the Guildmaster (1 Coin, 2 Flint). Works at: Lumber Camp.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.gua: Patrols, fights raiders, climbs ranks; with Guard Drill, spars by the Barracks at 07:00 for Strength and XP. Hire: Buy the Guard Emblem from the Guildmaster (3 Coins, 2 Iron Ingots, 1 Leather). Works at: Barracks.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.cou: Carries goods between the Banner, the Warehouse and the workshops. Hire: Buy the Courier Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 1 Chest, 2 Leather). Works at: Warehouse.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.bak: Bakes bread from wheat or flour at the Bakery. Hire: Buy the Baker Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 2 Bread, 1 Leather). Works at: Bakery.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.coo: Cooks mushroom stew, baked potatoes and dried kelp into meals at the Kitchen. Hire: Buy the Cook Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 2 Bowls, 1 Leather). Works at: Kitchen.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.but: Cooks raw beef, pork, mutton and chicken, and cures rabbit into Cured Hide. Hire: Buy the Butcher Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 1 Iron Ingot, 1 Leather). Works at: Butcher.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.sme: Smelts raw iron, copper and gold into ingots, and logs into charcoal. Hire: Buy the Smelter Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 1 Furnace, 1 Leather). Works at: Smelter.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.smi: Forges iron blooms into ingots and makes iron axes, pickaxes, hoes and swords. Hire: Buy the Smith Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 2 Iron Ingots, 1 Leather). Works at: Smithy.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.saw: Saws logs into planks and Timber Beams at the Sawmill. Hire: Buy the Sawyer Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 2 Iron Ingots, 2 Leather). Works at: Sawmill.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.car: Makes sticks, barrels and ladders from planks and Timber Beams. Hire: Buy the Carpenter Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 8 Sticks, 1 Leather). Works at: Carpenter.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.mas: Cuts cobblestone into stone and stone into stone bricks. Hire: Buy the Mason Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 16 Cobblestone, 1 Leather). Works at: Mason.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.fle: Makes arrows from flint or feathers, and bows from string. Hire: Buy the Fletcher Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 4 Feathers, 2 Flint). Works at: Fletcher.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.wea: Weaves Wool Bolts from any wool (white goes furthest), spins string into wool and sews banners. Hire: Buy the Weaver Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 4 String, 1 Leather). Works at: Weaver.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.tan: Tans Cured Hide and rabbit hide into leather. Hire: Buy the Tanner Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 2 Leather). Works at: Tannery.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.min: Digs a ladder shaft under the Mine, a short lane, then works the rock face: each swing can turn up coal, iron and more. With Deep Mine he goes deeper, where gold, redstone, lapis and even diamonds show up. Better pickaxes find better ore. Keep ladders and torches in the Mine chests. Hire: Buy the Miner Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 8 Torches, 1 Leather). Works at: Mine.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.inn: Runs the Tavern: serves ale and food to seated guests and cuts the recruit price. Hire: Buy the Innkeeper Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 2 Bread, 2 Leather). Works at: Tavern.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.sch: Studies at the Architect's Study to advance your chosen research project. Hire: Buy the Scholar Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 2 Books, 2 Leather). Works at: Architects Study.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.mil: Grinds wheat into flour and sugar cane into paper at the Mill. Hire: Buy the Miller Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 8 Wheat, 1 Leather). Works at: Mill.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.bre: Brews malt and ale from wheat at the Brewery. Hire: Buy the Brewer Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 2 Glass Bottles, 1 Leather). Works at: Brewery.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.arc: Shoots raiders from the Watchtower; ranks up to Master Archer with practice. Hire: Buy the Archer Emblem from the Guildmaster (3 Coins, 4 Arrows, 1 Leather). Works at: Watchtower.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.arm: Makes leather and iron armour for your soldiers at the Armoury. Hire: Buy the Armourer Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 2 Iron Ingots, 2 Leather). Works at: Armoury.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.her: Shears sheep, feeds and breeds animals and collects eggs in the Pasture. Hire: Buy the Herder Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 1 Hay Block, 1 Leather). Works at: Pasture.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.fis: Fishes from the shore chair for food and trade: casts the long Fisher's Rod, watches the float, strikes on the bite, reels the fish in and takes it off the line; with Fisher's Nets, also keeps a net and hauls it in. Hire: Buy the Fisher Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 2 String). Works at: Fishery.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.hun: Hunts wild game near the Lodge and brings back meat, hides and feathers. He stalks crouched with an arrow nocked, carries each kill home across his shoulders, then skins and butchers it at a Butchering Table, or kneeling on the Lodge floor when no table is free. Hire: Buy the Hunter Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 4 Flint, 8 Sticks). Works at: Hunters Lodge.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.tra: Sells surplus goods to merchants across the Trading Post counter; town chat reports each sale. Hire: Buy the Trade Steward Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 1 Chest, 4 Sticks). Works at: Trading Post.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.spe: Battle role: fights from the second rank with long reach and braces against charges. Hire: Buy the Spearman Emblem from the Guildmaster (4 Coins, 1 Iron Ingot, 1 Leather). Works at: Pike Yard.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.lon: Battle role: a two-handed swordsman who breaks shields and cuts through crowds. Hire: Buy the Longswordsman Emblem from the Guildmaster (5 Coins, 3 Iron Ingots, 2 Leather). Works at: Sword Hall.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.hea: Battle role: tends wounded soldiers in a fight and revives downed players. Hire: Buy the Healer Emblem from the Guildmaster (3 Coins, 2 Paper, 1 Leather). Works at: Infirmary.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.run: Battle role: spends rune charges on spells and wards that turn a fight. Hire: Buy the Rune Mage Emblem from the Guildmaster (6 Coins, 8 Lapis Lazuli, 4 Amethyst Shards, 1 Book). Works at: Rune Hall.
hearthstead.guide.ref.jobs_directory.bui: Builds blueprints, defense lines and Upgrade Orders from real delivered materials. Hire: Buy the Builder Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 2 Flint, 8 Sticks). Works at: Builders Hut.
hearthstead.guide.buildings_directory.li: Every building: what it is for, what the plaque checks, and its levels.
Right-click a plaque to see exactly what is still missing.
hearthstead.guide.ref.buildings_director: House

A home: every bed you add lets one more settler live in the village. Room. Needs: 1 bed, 1 door, 1 light, 9 floor. Levels (by hand or by Upgrade Order): L2 2 lights, 1 storage, solid floor; L3 3 lights, 1 storage, solid floor, 3 furnishing, 1 crafting table; L4 5 lights, 2 storage, solid floor, 6 furnishing, 1 crafting table, 25 floor.
Lodging House

A shared bunk house for up to 8 settlers. Room. Needs: 4 beds, 1 door, 2 lights, 24 floor. Levels (by hand or by Upgrade Order): L2 4 lights, 2 storage, solid floor; L3 6 beds, 6 lights, 2 storage, solid floor.
Warehouse

The shared store Couriers fill and empty; higher levels manage more containers. Room. Needs: 4 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 25 floor. Levels (by hand or by Upgrade Order): L2 16 storage, 1 ledger desk, 4 lights, 1 door, 25 floor, solid floor; L3 32 storage, 1 ledger desk, 4 signs, 6 lights, 1 door, 100 floor, solid floor; L4 64 storage, 1 ledger desk, 8 signs, 10 lights, 2 doors, 200 floor, solid floor; L5 128 storage, 2 ledger desks, 16 signs, 16 lights, 2 doors, 320 floor, solid floor.
Architect's Study
The Scholar's study, where your chosen research project advances. Room. Needs: 1 lectern, 2 bookshelves, 1 door, 2 lights, 16 floor.
School
With Families & School learned, newcomers arrive one trade level higher (3 in all). Room. Needs: 4 bookshelves, 2 lecterns, 1 door, 2 lights, 25 floor.
Farmhouse

Base for the Farmer, who works the fields you mark with the Work Scepter. Room. Needs: 1 composter, 1 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 16 floor. Levels (by hand or by Upgrade Order): L2 2 storage, 3 lights (+1 worker from L2).
Mill
The Miller grinds wheat into flour and sugar cane into paper. Room. Needs: 1 grindstone, 2 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 16 floor.
Bakery
The Baker turns wheat or flour into bread. Room. Needs: 2 furnace/smoker, 1 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 16 floor.
Kitchen
The Cook turns mushrooms, potatoes and kelp into ready meals. Room. Needs: 1 furnace/smoker, 1 cauldron, 2 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 20 floor.
Dining Hall
Settlers gather here at mealtime; it cuts the recruit price. Room. Needs: 1 campfire, 1 storage, 1 door, 3 lights, 36 floor.
Pasture
A paddock you stock with animals; the Herder shears, breeds and collects eggs. Room. Needs: 2 hay bales, 1 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 25 floor.
Butcher
The Butcher cooks raw meat and cures rabbit into Cured Hide. Room. Needs: 1 smoker, 2 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 16 floor.
Fishery

A Fishery needs a chair beside at least 20 connected surface-water cells, a rack, barrel, door, light and 16 floor cells. Fishery blueprints include an indoor basin. After construction, bring two water buckets to establish a refillable source and fill the basin; the plan does not leave it filled. Keep the chair facing source water and recheck the plaque.
Hunter's Lodge
The Hunter's base: game is hunted nearby and butchered here. Room. Needs: 1 fletching table, 1 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 16 floor.
Brewery
The Brewer makes malt and ale from wheat. Room. Needs: 1 brewing stand, 1 cauldron, 2 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 16 floor.
Tavern

The Innkeeper serves ale and food here; travellers visit and can be recruited. Room. Needs: 1 bell, 2 storage, 1 ale tap, 1 door, 3 lights, 36 floor. Levels (by hand or by Upgrade Order): L2 5 lights, 4 seats (stairs), solid floor.
Well House
While a valid Well House stands, every settler with a bed gets +2 morale. Work yard (outdoor area). Needs: Yard or room: 4 water, 1 door, 1 light, 9 floor.
Lumber Camp

Base for the Lumberer, who fells trees in the area you mark. Work yard (outdoor area). Needs: Yard or room: 1 crafting table, 1 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 16 floor. Levels (by hand or by Upgrade Order): L2 1 sawbench (stonecutter), 2 storage, 4 lights (+1 worker from L2).
Sawmill
The Sawyer turns logs into planks and Timber Beams. Work yard (outdoor area). Needs: Yard or room: 1 stonecutter, 2 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 20 floor.
Carpenter's Shop
The Carpenter makes sticks, barrels and ladders. Room. Needs: 2 crafting tables, 2 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 20 floor.
Mine Entrance

The Miner digs a ladder shaft down from the ladder at the shaft mouth, then works the rock face at the end of a short lane. Keep ladders and torches in the Mine chests. Work yard (outdoor area). Needs: Yard or room: 3 ladders, 2 storage, 1 door, 3 lights, 20 floor.
Smelter
The Smelter turns raw ore into ingots and logs into charcoal. Work yard (outdoor area). Needs: Yard or room: 2 furnaces, 2 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 20 floor.
Smithy
The Smith forges ingots and iron tools and swords. Work yard (outdoor area). Needs: Yard or room: 1 anvil, 1 smithing table, 1 furnace, 2 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 20 floor.
Weaver's Cottage
The Weaver makes wool, Wool Bolts and banners. Room. Needs: 1 loom, 1 cauldron, 2 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 16 floor.
Infirmary
The Healer's post; with the Infirmary node, wounded settlers inside heal steadily. Room. Needs: 1 cauldron, 2 beds, 1 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 20 floor.
Barracks

Home post of your Guards: they sleep, gear up and turn out from here. Room. Needs: 2 beds, 2 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 36 floor. Levels (by hand or by Upgrade Order): L2 4 beds, 4 lights, solid floor.
Watchtower
Archers shoot from here, and Guards can be posted on the tower. Room. Needs: 4 ladders, 1 storage, 1 door, 4 lights, 9 floor. Levels (by hand or by Upgrade Order): L2 6 ladders, 6 lights.
Tannery
The Tanner turns hides into leather. Work yard (outdoor area). Needs: Yard or room: 2 cauldrons, 2 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 16 floor.
Fletcher
The Fletcher makes arrows and bows. Room. Needs: 1 fletching table, 1 crafting table, 2 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 16 floor.
Armoury
The Armourer makes leather and iron armour for your soldiers. Room. Needs: 1 smithing table, 4 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 25 floor.
Mason's Yard
The Mason cuts cobblestone into stone and stone bricks. Work yard (outdoor area). Needs: Yard or room: 8 stone bricks, 2 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 20 floor.
Library
Makes every research project 25% cheaper in materials. Room. Needs: 8 bookshelves, 1 lectern, 1 door, 3 lights, 25 floor.
Market
While a valid Market stands, visiting merchants carry 6 more Coins. Work yard (outdoor area). Needs: Yard or room: 4 stalls (barrel or scaffold), 2 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 36 floor.
Trading Post

The Trader's shop. Set the counter in the front wall with air above it; merchants buy outside. Work yard (outdoor area). Needs: Yard or room: 1 scaffold or cartography table, 2 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 16 floor.
Builder's Hut

The Builder's hut: materials are delivered here and the Builder builds your orders. Work yard (outdoor area). Needs: Yard or room: 1 crafting table, 2 storage, 1 door, 1 light, 16 floor. Levels (by hand or by Upgrade Order): L2 4 storage, 2 lights, 25 floor, solid floor; L3 8 storage, 4 lights, 36 floor, solid floor, 2 crafting tables.
Pike Yard
Drill yard and bunks for Spearmen. Room. Needs: 2 beds, 2 hay bales, 1 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 30 floor.
Sword Hall
Drill hall and bunks for Longswordsmen. Room. Needs: 2 beds, 1 anvil, 1 grindstone, 1 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 30 floor.
Rune Hall
Where Rune Mages study and carve their runes. Room. Needs: 1 enchanting table, 4 amethyst blocks, 4 bookshelves, 1 door, 3 lights, 25 floor.
hearthstead.guide.events_directory.list1: Everything that can happen around your settlement, and what to do about it.
Watch for the ! marker on the realm map.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.p: The peddler greets you and opens his wares. Choose Trade to open the barter table, or leave.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.r: The refugee family asks to be taken in. Accept, ask them to work (a Charisma roll), give food, or decline.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.m: The minstrel troupe offers to play at your Tavern. Host the feast for Coins, let them play for tips, or send them away.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.f: A fox sneaks into your fields and steals ripe crops. Chase it off; your Farmer runs out and a Hunter can shoot it to drop the crop.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.w: Three wolves come for your livestock at night. Guards fight them; the pack leaves after one kill or two losses and is gone by dawn.
A bad-tempered boar roots up crops in your fields. Let Guards fight it or have a Hunter shoot it for extra meat.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.t: Two settlers fall out over ale and come to blows (no real damage). Right-click a brawler to break it up, or a Guard will; each ending costs a little morale.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.b: The brute chief demands a toll of food. Pay food or Coins, try to talk them down (Intimidation; pointing at your walls only works if you have walls or guards), refuse, or attack.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.s: Stray Dog (talk)
The stray dog looks up at you hopefully. Feed it to adopt it, or shoo it away.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.c: The caravan master offers trade or asks for an escort. Barter, agree to escort them past the woods, or let them pass.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.r: The rival lord's envoy states his master's business. Negotiate a pact (a trade roll), befriend with a gift, insult, or dismiss.
After the first raid, a raid comes every 3-4 in-game days; the warning sounds at dusk the evening before. Arm and post your Guards and Archers, keep the Banner stocked, and fight beside them.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.g: Now and then a Goblin Thief sneaks in to pickpocket (at most 1 Coin from a poor purse), then runs rather than fights. Chase it down before it escapes; it sometimes drops goblin loot. Like other hostile visitors, it leaves a young village alone for its first days.
hearthstead.guide.ref.events_directory.e: A merchant regularly walks to the Banner and buys your goods for Coins from a limited purse. Sell goods to earn the Coins you spend on tech nodes, emblems and recruits.
hearthstead.guide.tech_branches.crown1.b: Every node of the Crown branch and what it gives you.
hearthstead.guide.tech_branches.crown1.t: Open the Banner, then Tech Tree, to learn a node.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.sett: Found your hamlet: 4 founders, the Guildmaster by the Banner and ring 1 of every branch.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.firs: Survive your first raid and the hamlet becomes a Village: ring 2 opens in every branch, and your guards may wear mail.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.town: Become a Town: ring 3 opens and visiting merchants bring fuller purses.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.cast: Become a Castle: ring 4 opens, merchants bring fuller purses again, and with the Master Armoury your best fighters may wear diamond.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.king: Crown yourself: Kingdom rank, the fullest merchant purses, and with the Master Armoury your captains may wear netherite.
hearthstead.guide.tech_branches.watch1.b: Every node of the Watch & Defense branch and what it gives you.
hearthstead.guide.tech_branches.watch1.t: Open the Banner, then Tech Tree, to learn a node.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.firs: Build a Barracks and hire Guards who patrol, answer the alarm and fight beside you.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.guar: Guards spar in pairs each morning after the night watch and earn +15% combat XP.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.arm_: Build a Watchtower, hire Archers, and post Guards on the tower.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.comm: Your captain's voice carries: orders reach soldiers up to 80 blocks away instead of 48, raid orders hold 60 seconds after the raid instead of 30, and every order sounds a horn that rallies the listeners (+10% speed for 10 seconds).
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.barr: When a raid is spotted, every Builder drops other work to raise your marked barricades first, and barricade lines may be twice as long.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.defe: Draw a defense line on the ground and your Builder raises palisade walls, gates and a timber watchtower along it.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.shie: Guards holding a line with a shield take 30% less damage from the front, and earn +25% combat XP.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.spea: A new battle role: Spearmen fight from the second rank with long reach and brace against charges.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.guar: Veterans wear iron chest and legs, Sergeants full iron: one armour tier earlier.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.arch: Archers shoot 2 blocks farther and draw their bows faster.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.cros: Archers switch to heavy bolts: each shot takes 50% longer to draw, but every hit does 40% more damage.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.fort: An Armourer forges armour and shields for your guards from village iron and leather.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.watc: When the alarm sounds, villagers run for shelter 25% faster.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.pali: Your palisade becomes a fighting wall: raiders need twice as many blows to break a palisade segment.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.eart: Raiders within 3 blocks of your built defense lines are slowed (Slowness II, 30% slower).
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.ston: Stone wall segments take three times as many blows to break.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.vete: Guards master their moveset: the shield bash is ready 30% sooner, the combo window is 4 ticks longer, and heavy strikes hit 30% harder.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.capt: Your highest-ranked guard is field-promoted to Sergeant and commissioned Captain: bigger and stronger, a chosen weapon loadout with special attacks, and your soldiers salute him.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.long: A new battle role: two-handed longswordsmen who break shields and cut through crowds.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.rune: A new battle role: a Rune Mage who spends rune charges on spells that turn a fight.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.mast: Your guards and archers may wear diamond (Gear Tier 3, with the Castle Charter) and netherite (Gear Tier 4, with the Kingdom Crown).
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.high: Your mages master the high runes: a second Rune Mage may be hired, and wards last 6 seconds instead of 5.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.knig: Order of Knights: your Sergeants and Captains fight as knights, +25% damage and no knockback.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.pike: Spearmen doctrine: braced Spearmen strike 50% harder and cannot be knocked back.
hearthstead.guide.tech_branches.logistic: Every node of the Logistics branch and what it gives you.
Open the Banner, then Tech Tree, to learn a node.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.stor: Build a Warehouse and hire Couriers who carry goods to one shared store.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.stou: Couriers carry 2 more items on every trip, and a Courier with room left takes one more nearby pickup on the same trip.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.pave: Every settler walks 15% faster on roads: dirt path, gravel, cobble, stone and bricks.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.cour: Sack tier 1: Couriers carry 50% more (8 -> 12 per trip), and you can see the bigger sack on their back.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.leat: Sack tier 2: Couriers carry double (8 -> 16 per trip).
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.fram: Sack tier 3: Couriers carry 2.5x (8 -> 20 per trip).
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.hand: Couriers push a real, visible hand cart: +200% carry.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.work: Lumberers and Farmers carry at the settlement's sack tier (at least +50%).
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.ware: The plaque now recognises Warehouse level 3, the Storehouse: 64 managed containers.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.cour: Couriers serve Urgent, then High, then Normal requests, whatever the kind: Banner food goes before workshop inputs.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.cost: Cart tier 2: the Courier's cart carries +300% of the base load instead of +200%, and looks it.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.port: Heavy loads: Couriers carry 50% more on every trip, but walk 10% slower.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.runn: Swift feet: Couriers walk 15% faster and try a blocked route again twice as soon.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.grea: The plaque now recognises the Great Storehouse: 128 managed containers for a town's worth of goods.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.mule: Cart tier 3: the Courier's cart carries +400% of the base load and rolls 20% faster on roads.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.roya: The plaque now recognises the Royal Storehouse: 256 managed containers, the granary of a castle.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.cara: Trade caravans come to your Banner far more often: at least every 3 days, and 3x as likely on other event days.
hearthstead.guide.tech_branches.commons1: Every node of the Commons & Household branch and what it gives you.
Open the Banner, then Tech Tree, to learn a node.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.home: Build Houses and a Lodging; every bed beyond the 4 founders lets one more settler live here.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.warm: Warm homes keep hunger down at night, and an evening by the Banner fire lifts everyone's spirits.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.hosp: With 3 living settlers, learn Tavern & Inn and build a Tavern; an Innkeeper serves meals and ale and draws recruits. Beds are not required for this research.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.stur: Better beds: settlers with a claimed bed get +2 morale, and +2 more in a well-kept home.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.feat: Settlers who sleep a calm night in a bed wake Well Rested and can do 10% more work that day.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.hear: A Scholar researches upgrades you choose, a Library makes every project cheaper, and study goes faster.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.bard: The bard plays to a crowd: evening morale lifts higher, and visiting travellers tip Coins.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.kitc: Build a Kitchen and a Dining Hall, and hire a Cook to feed the village.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.war_: When a raid is warned and the stores hold 12 meals and 4 ale, the village feasts: guards fight 10% harder and hold their nerve that night.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.two_: Townhouses: every House may hold two more settlers (bed cap 4 -> 6), and a House furnished to level 3 is a Townhouse.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.ways: A small chapel: after every raid you hold, the village gives thanks and everyone's morale lifts.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.aleh: A proper alehouse: build a Brewery, hire a Brewer, and a pint lifts spirits more than ever.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.infi: Build an Infirmary: wounded settlers inside heal steadily.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.mano: Manors: every House may hold two more settlers again, and a House furnished to level 4 becomes a Manor whose residents are happier.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.grea: Your Tavern becomes a famous inn: minstrels and trade caravans visit twice as often.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.harv: Every 4 days at dawn the village holds a Harvest Feast: +15 morale and faster workshops for a day.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.hall: Honour the fallen: the village grieves half as much, and newcomers arrive in better spirits.
School: new settlers arrive already trained, one level ahead in every trade.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.batt: Hire Healers: they tend wounded soldiers in a fight and revive downed players.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.cath: A cathedral rises over the town: after every raid you hold, the whole village's morale soars.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.hall: The greatest hall in the land: the house matches every Coin travellers pay for meals, and the bard lifts spirits twice as high.
hearthstead.guide.tech_branches.craft1.b: Every node of the Craft & Production branch and what it gives you.
hearthstead.guide.tech_branches.craft1.t: Open the Banner, then Tech Tree, to learn a node.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.timb: Build a Lumber Camp, hire a Lumberer, and get the Work Scepter.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.buil: Hire a Builder: they fill the gaps on any building's checklist, build blueprints for you, and lay barricade lines.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.shar: Lumberers fell each tree 10% faster, and every 8 trees they whet the axe at the camp grindstone.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.cult: Build a Farmhouse and hire a Farmer who sows, reaps and stores wheat.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.shor: Build a Fishery; a Fisher lands food from day one, and rare catches for trade.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.fish: Casts finish 10% sooner, and the Fisher keeps a net in the water: 1 fish an hour, up to 4.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.guil: A Sawyer turns logs into planks and Timber Beams.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.land: Millers, Bakers, Herders and Butchers: bread in bulk, wool, leather and meat.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.bord: A Hunter ranges beyond the walls and brings back meat, feathers and hides.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.tann: A Tanner cures hides into leather and Cured Hide.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.craf: Mine ore, smelt iron and forge tools. Lumberers and Miners holding an iron tool work 10% faster (diamond or netherite: 20%).
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.maso: Your Builder learns stone: stone wall segments, a stone gatehouse, a stone watchtower, and stone floors in Upgrade Orders.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.carp: Workshops for furniture, stone bricks and Wool Bolts, the stuff towns are built from.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.char: Every Smelter batch takes 25% less time and 25% less effort, so a Smelter finishes more ingots and charcoal a day.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.deep: The Miner digs his shaft further down to a second level, where the rock face gives more iron and gold, plus redstone, lapis and rare diamonds. 15% of the ore he finds gives 1 extra ore.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.mast: Workers who share a workshop with a master (trade level 5+) earn 50% more trade XP.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.guil: Crafted goods roll their quality as if the crafter were 2 trade levels higher: Fine or better far more often.
Every node of the Development (legacy) common branch and what it gives you.
Open the Banner, then Tech Tree, to learn a node.
hearthstead.guide.ref.tech_branches.shel: Founding milestone, granted free with the Charter: ready the foundation to open the first ring of jobs and houses
hearthstead.guide.options.controls.title: Controls
hearthstead.guide.options.controls.b1: Every Bannerhold key. Change them in Options, Controls, Bannerhold.
hearthstead.guide.options.controls.tip: The Handbook shows your own keys, even after you change them.
hearthstead.guide.options.switches1.b1: Server owners can turn whole systems off in hearthstead-server.toml, [features].
hearthstead.guide.options.switches1.tip: Turn a system off if it breaks on your server; your world keeps its data.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_b: Off: Builders, build orders and the Builder's Plan stop working. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_w: Off: no world events (peddler, refugees, wolves and the rest) start. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_b: Off: Spearmen, Longswordsmen, Healers and Rune Mages cannot be hired or fight. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_g: Off: the command keys and summoning settlers stop working. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_w: Off: no Warehouse levels, sorting or warehouse index. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_g: Off: no settler gear tiers or tiered armour looks. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_c: Off: settlers, visitors and raiders use the old plain skins. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_l: Off: no sack tiers, hand carts or road speed bonus. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_c: Off: no talk screens; visitors answer in chat and raids never parley. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_e: Off: hides the 4 specialization nodes and 15 trade emblems. Existing workers keep going. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_l: Off: settlers stop greeting, barking lines, sheltering from rain and cheering. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_p: Off: Guard squads walk ordinary rounds instead of your Patrol Map routes. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features_c: Off: short sword, double axe, halberd and warhammer lose their special traits. Default: true.
hearthstead.guide.options.sections1.b1: What each section of the config files controls.
hearthstead.guide.options.sections1.tip: Change settings with the game closed, then restart.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.time.name: [time]
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.builder.te: skipUnsuppliedDecor (default on): the Builder leaves out decoration nobody in the village makes (flowers, leaves, cobwebs, amethyst...) and builds coloured beds, wool, carpets and banners in white. Off: every blueprint exactly as drawn.
hearthstead.guide.builder.supply.title: Village supplies
hearthstead.guide.builder.supply.b1: Unlocked, staffed workshops can craft missing blocks when they know the recipe. Otherwise the Builder asks for your help.
hearthstead.guide.builder.supply.b2: Carpenter: stairs, slabs, fences, doors, chests. Mason: stone shapes, furnaces, glass panes. Smith: plaques, lanterns.
hearthstead.guide.builder.supply.b3: Smelter: glass and bricks. Sawyer: dark oak planks. Miller: hay bales. Weaver: white beds and carpets.
hearthstead.guide.builder.supply.b4: Decoration nobody can make (flowers, leaves, cobwebs) is left out; coloured beds and wool are built white.
hearthstead.guide.builder.supply.tip: Unlock and staff the workshop, or bring the missing blocks. A request for you is not counted as incoming stock.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.settlement: radius (default 72, 32-80): claim of a newly founded town in blocks from the Banner. Sets the raid ring, defended area, patrols, Builder area and Banner spacing. A saved town keeps its radius.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.debug.name: [debug]
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.hunting.te: 7 settings, e.g. huntingGrounds, gameCap, spawnIntervalSeconds, minPlayerDistance ….
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.raids.name: [raids]
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.raids.text: 7 settings, e.g. recurringRaidMinDays, recurringRaidMaxDays, skirmisherBaseHealth, bruteBaseHealth ….
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.combat.tex: 18 settings, e.g. guardLightDamageMultiplier, guardHeavyDamageMultiplier, guardFinisherDamageMultiplier, guardShieldBashDamageMultiplier ….
4 settings: handCartPercent, handCartRoughPercent, pavedRoadsPercent and courierBatching (below).
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.logistics_: On by default. Stout Straps pickup batching: after lifting one load, a Courier with room left takes one more waiting pickup within 16 blocks and delivers both on the same trip. Off: one request per trip, as before; a trip already under way still finishes.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.raid.name: [raid]
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.raid.text: firstRaidAutoDays (default 3): days from founding to the first timed raid, with advance warning. firstRaidMinimalSize (default 3, range 2-3): weak raiders without defenders. preFirstRaidMealReserve (default 16): ready-meal reserve cap before the first raid ends.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.pathing.te: stuckWatchdog (default on): a settler that wants to walk but has not moved re-plans after 10 s and steps off an awkward spot after 20 s. rescueAfterSeconds (default 90, 30-600): a settler shut in that long is moved to the nearest open spot with a way to the Banner, at most once per 5 minutes, never during a raid; no block changes. rescueChat (default on): one town chat line per rescue. routeHome (default off): after 45 s, drop the task and walk home.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.start.name: [start]
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.start.text: kitBread (default 0): optional extra first-join bread with the Handbook; the Guildmaster's welcome gives each player 16 bread with their iron tools. startCoins (default 0): physical Coins put in the Banner once per successful village founding; 0 disables the grant. Rejoining an existing Banner gives no extra Coins. The Guildmaster's welcome (4 Coins once per village, iron tools and 16 bread once per player) is separate and not a config option.
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.chat.name: [chat]
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.chat.text: Town chat: one short line per important event, only to the town's members (players who used its Banner), as [Town name]. One switch each, all on: raid (red), death (dark red), building and upgrade (green), research (gold), trade (aqua).
hearthstead.guide.ref.options.revive.tex: 7 settings, e.g. enabled, soloDowned, bleedOutSeconds, reviveSeconds ….

hearthstead.guide.ref.options.features.t: 13 settings, e.g. builder, worldEvents, battleRoles, guardCommands ….
