hearthstead.howto.banner.use: Place it to found your settlement; right-click it to open it.
hearthstead.howto.banner.s1: Place it on open ground with 2 free blocks above it.
hearthstead.howto.banner.s2: Right-click it to open the Banner screen.
hearthstead.howto.banner.s3: Sneak + right-click to open its storage.
hearthstead.howto.banner.s4: Right-click it holding a banner to copy that banner's colours.
hearthstead.howto.handbook.use: Right-click to read the Settler's Handbook.
hearthstead.howto.handbook.s1: Right-click in the air to open the Handbook.
hearthstead.howto.handbook.s2: Sneak + right-click to ask what your settlement stores.
hearthstead.howto.handbook.s3: Or press the Handbook key anywhere.
hearthstead.howto.handbook.obtain: You get one when you first join; you can also craft it from a book and a sapling.
hearthstead.howto.plaque.use: Hang it in a room, then fit a Build Plan to make it a building.
hearthstead.howto.plaque.s1: Hang it on a wall inside the room.
hearthstead.howto.plaque.s2: Right-click it holding a Build Plan to set the building.
hearthstead.howto.plaque.s3: Right-click with an empty hand to see its checklist.
hearthstead.howto.plaque.s4: Sneak + right-click with an empty hand to take the plan back.
hearthstead.howto.build_plan.use: Use it on a blank Plaque to set what the building is.
hearthstead.howto.build_plan.s1: Learn the building in the Tech Tree: its plan recipe unlocks.
hearthstead.howto.build_plan.s2: Craft it: paper, a feather and the building's token item.
hearthstead.howto.build_plan.s3: Right-click a blank Plaque with it.
hearthstead.howto.build_plan.obtain: Crafted; each building's plan recipe unlocks when you learn it in the Tech Tree.
hearthstead.howto.work_scepter.use: Marks the area a Lumberer or Farmer works in.
hearthstead.howto.work_scepter.s1: Hold it and right-click the Lumber Camp or Farmhouse plaque.
hearthstead.howto.work_scepter.s2: Right-click two ground corners around the work area.
hearthstead.howto.work_scepter.s3: Right-click once more at the height you want.
hearthstead.howto.work_scepter.s4: Check the outlined box and press Confirm Zone.
hearthstead.howto.builders_plan.use: Right-click to order buildings, walls and upgrades from your Builder.
hearthstead.howto.builders_plan.s1: Right-click in the air to open the Plan.
hearthstead.howto.builders_plan.s2: Pick a blueprint: a ghost follows your aim. Scroll rotates it.
hearthstead.howto.builders_plan.s3: Right-click to check the spot, then press Confirm.
hearthstead.howto.builders_plan.s4: Needs a Builder's Hut with a hired Builder.
hearthstead.howto.survey_rod.use: Copies a structure you built into Our Designs.
hearthstead.howto.survey_rod.s2: Right-click the opposite corner block (max 32 per side).
hearthstead.howto.survey_rod.s3: Name it: it appears under Our Designs in the Builder's Plan.
hearthstead.howto.resource_scroll.use: Shows what a Builder's site needs and what is missing.
hearthstead.howto.resource_scroll.s1: Right-click a Builder's Hut plaque to link the scroll.
hearthstead.howto.resource_scroll.s2: Right-click anywhere to see needs, stock and what is on the way.
hearthstead.howto.patrol_map.use: Draws a patrol route for your guards.
hearthstead.howto.patrol_map.s1: Right-click the ground to add the next waypoint.
hearthstead.howto.patrol_map.s2: Click waypoint 1 again to close the loop.
hearthstead.howto.patrol_map.s3: Sneak + right-click a marker to remove it.
hearthstead.howto.patrol_map.s4: Right-click the air to choose guards and shifts.
hearthstead.howto.job_emblem.use: Right-click a settler to give them this job.
hearthstead.howto.job_emblem.s1: Buy it: right-click the Guildmaster beside the Banner.
hearthstead.howto.job_emblem.s2: Hold it in your main hand.
hearthstead.howto.job_emblem.s3: Right-click a settler without sneaking to hire them.
hearthstead.howto.job_emblem.s4: It is only used up if the hire works.
hearthstead.howto.job_emblem.obtain: Bought from the Guildmaster beside the Banner (Professions & Emblems) once its Tech Tree node is learned. Firing a worker returns it.
hearthstead.howto.blessing_seal.use: Sneak + right-click a settler or a plaque to bless it.
hearthstead.howto.blessing_seal.s1: Win a raid, then right-click the Banner and pick a seal.
hearthstead.howto.blessing_seal.s2: Sneak + right-click a settler or a building's plaque.
hearthstead.howto.blessing_seal.s3: It is only used up if the blessing binds.
hearthstead.howto.blessing_seal.obtain: A reward you choose at the Banner after winning a raid.
hearthstead.howto.coin.use: The settlement's money: knowledge, emblems and recruits cost Coins.
hearthstead.howto.coin.s1: Sell goods to the Traveling Merchant at the Banner.
hearthstead.howto.coin.s2: Win raids and help events for more Coins.
hearthstead.howto.coin.s3: Payments take from you, the Banner, then Warehouse chests.
hearthstead.howto.coin.obtain: Selling goods to the merchant, raid victories and world events pay Coins.
hearthstead.howto.role_weapon.use: A spear for you, or for your Spearmen.
hearthstead.howto.role_weapon.s1: Fight with it yourself: spears reach 1 block farther.
hearthstead.howto.role_weapon.s2: Or put it in a Warehouse chest.
hearthstead.howto.role_weapon.s3: A Courier brings it to the soldier who asks for it.
hearthstead.howto.bandage.use: Hold right-click to heal 8 health over 8 seconds.
hearthstead.howto.bandage.s1: When hurt, hold right-click for 1.5 seconds.
hearthstead.howto.bandage.s2: Healers carry bandages and restock from the Infirmary or Warehouse.
hearthstead.howto.rune_stone.use: Refills a Rune Mage's spell charges.
hearthstead.howto.rune_stone.s1: Put rune stones in the Rune Hall or a Warehouse chest.
hearthstead.howto.rune_stone.s2: Rune Mages fetch them to refill their charges.
hearthstead.howto.fishers_rod.use: The Fisher's tool: they cannot fish without it.
hearthstead.howto.fishers_rod.s1: Put it in a Warehouse chest; a Courier brings it to the Fisher.
hearthstead.howto.fishers_rod.s2: You can fish with it yourself too.
hearthstead.howto.fishers_chair.use: The Fisher sits on it, facing the water.
hearthstead.howto.fishers_chair.s1: Place it in the Fishery by the water.
hearthstead.howto.fish_rack.use: Holds and shows off the Fisher's catch.
hearthstead.howto.fish_rack.s1: Place it in the Fishery: a Fishery needs one.
hearthstead.howto.fish_rack.s2: Right-click to store up to 4 fish.
hearthstead.howto.ale_tap.use: Pours ale: right-click with a glass bottle and a Coin.
hearthstead.howto.ale_tap.s1: Place it on a wall with a barrel right behind it.
hearthstead.howto.ale_tap.s3: Right-click holding a glass bottle: it takes 1 Coin.
hearthstead.howto.butchering_table.use: Where your Hunter butchers carcasses quickly.
hearthstead.howto.butchering_table.s1: Place it inside the Hunter's Lodge.
hearthstead.howto.butchering_table.s2: Right-click holding a carcass to lay it down.
hearthstead.howto.butchering_table.s3: Right-click with an empty hand to take it back.
hearthstead.howto.goods.use: Trade goods: made in a workshop, used by the next one or sold.
hearthstead.howto.goods.s1: Your workers make it in their workshop.
hearthstead.howto.goods.s2: Couriers carry it to where it is needed.
hearthstead.howto.goods.s3: The Traveling Merchant buys many goods for Coins.
hearthstead.howto.goods.obtain: Made by your Miller, Brewer, Innkeeper, Smelter, Sawyer, Butcher or Weaver.
hearthstead.howto.fish.use: Caught by your Fisher: eat it, sell it or turn it into meals.
hearthstead.howto.fish.s1: Put plain fish in the Banner: it cuts them into Fish Portions.
hearthstead.howto.fish.s2: Graded fish are for selling, not for meals.
hearthstead.howto.fish.s3: The merchant pays well for the better fish.
hearthstead.howto.fish.obtain: Caught by a Fisher settler; Fish Portions are made in the Banner.
hearthstead.howto.carcass.use: An animal your Hunter shot, waiting to be butchered.
hearthstead.howto.carcass.s1: The Hunter carries it home and butchers it.
hearthstead.howto.carcass.s2: On a Butchering Table it goes much faster.
hearthstead.howto.carcass.obtain: Only from animals your Hunter shoots.
hearthstead.howto.goblin_loot.use: Goblin loot. The stick poisons; the toenail is best not eaten.
hearthstead.howto.goblin_loot.s1: Hit an enemy with the stick: poison for 5 seconds.
hearthstead.howto.goblin_loot.s2: Eating the toenail drops you to half a heart.
hearthstead.howto.spawn_egg.use: Right-click the ground to spawn a settler.
hearthstead.howto.spawn_egg.s1: Right-click the ground where the settler should appear.
hearthstead.guide.items.banner.title: The Banner
hearthstead.guide.items.banner.b1: The heart of your settlement: everything is counted from it.
hearthstead.guide.items.banner.tip: Place it where you want the town square.
hearthstead.guide.items.handbook.title: The Handbook
hearthstead.guide.items.handbook.b1: This book. You get one when you first join.
hearthstead.guide.items.handbook.tip: Lost it? Craft a new one from a book and any sapling.
hearthstead.guide.items.plaque.title: Plaque and Build Plans
hearthstead.guide.items.plaque.b1: A Plaque turns a room into a building once a plan is fitted.
hearthstead.guide.items.plaque.tip: Hang the plaque first, then build the room around its checklist.
hearthstead.guide.items.work_scepter.b1: Draws the Work Zone your Lumberers and Farmers work in.
hearthstead.guide.items.work_scepter.tip: Draw a zone around a few whole trees.
hearthstead.guide.items.builders_plan.b1: Your order book for the Builder: buildings, walls and upgrades.
hearthstead.guide.items.builders_plan.ti: Check the Sites tab when a Builder seems stuck.
hearthstead.guide.items.survey_rod.title: Survey Rod
hearthstead.guide.items.survey_rod.b1: Save something you built so the Builder can build it again.
hearthstead.guide.items.survey_rod.tip: Click blocks, not the air: two corners, then a name.
Your Builder's shopping list, readable anywhere.
Link it once, then check it before a supply run.
hearthstead.guide.items.patrol_map.title: Patrol Map
hearthstead.guide.items.patrol_map.b1: Draw a route your guards walk on their shift.
hearthstead.guide.items.patrol_map.tip: Close the loop by clicking the first marker again.
hearthstead.guide.items.emblems.title: Job Emblems
hearthstead.guide.items.emblems.b1: An Emblem is a job contract: give it to a settler to hire them.
hearthstead.guide.items.emblems.tip: Prices are listed under More detail.
hearthstead.guide.items.emblems.prices: Prices at the Guildmaster (Coins first, then goods): Lumberer 1 + 2 flint. Farmer 2 + 8 seeds + 1 leather. Fisher 2 + 2 string + 1 leather. Courier 2 + chest + 2 leather. Trader 2 + 2 paper + 2 leather. Innkeeper 2 + 2 bread + 2 leather. Guard 3 + 2 iron + 1 leather. Archer 3 + 4 arrows + 1 leather. Hunter 2 + 12 arrows + 2 leather. Sawyer 2 + 2 iron + 2 leather. Scholar 2 + 2 books + 2 leather. Builder 2 + 2 flint + 8 sticks. Spearman 4 + 1 iron + 1 leather. Longswordsman 5 + 3 iron + 2 leather. Healer 3 + 2 paper + 1 leather. Rune Mage 6 + 8 lapis + 4 amethyst + 1 book. Other trades cost 2 Coins plus a trade item: Miller 8 wheat, Herder hay, Baker 2 bread, Butcher iron, Miner 8 torches, Smelter furnace, Smith 2 iron, Tanner 2 leather, Carpenter 8 sticks, Mason 16 cobblestone, Weaver 4 string, Cook 2 bowls, Brewer 2 bottles, Armourer 2 iron, Fletcher 4 feathers (most also 1 leather). Each Emblem is sold once its Tech Tree node is learned.
hearthstead.guide.items.seals.title: Blessing Seals
hearthstead.guide.items.seals.b1: A raid victory lets you pick one seal: a lasting blessing.
hearthstead.guide.items.seals.tip: Bless your best defender or the Barracks.
hearthstead.guide.items.coins.title: Coins
hearthstead.guide.items.coins.b1: Real items, and the only money in Bannerhold.
hearthstead.guide.items.coins.tip: Keep spare Coins in the Banner: purchases can take them from there.
hearthstead.guide.items.weapons.title: Spears
hearthstead.guide.items.weapons.b1: Spears for you and for your Spearmen.
hearthstead.guide.items.weapons.tip: Stock one spare weapon per soldier in the Warehouse.
Supplies your Healers and Rune Mages use up.
Keep a stack of each in the Warehouse before a raid.
hearthstead.guide.items.fishery.title: Fishery gear
hearthstead.guide.items.fishery.b1: A Fishery needs a chair and a rack; the Fisher needs the rod.
hearthstead.guide.items.fishery.tip: Put the chair right at the water's edge.
hearthstead.guide.items.workplace.title: Ale Tap and Butchering Table
hearthstead.guide.items.workplace.b1: Workplace blocks for the Tavern and the Hunter's Lodge.
hearthstead.guide.items.workplace.tip: The tap needs a barrel directly behind it.
hearthstead.guide.items.goods.title: Trade goods
hearthstead.guide.items.goods.b1: Flour, malt, ale, iron bloom, beams, hides and wool bolts.
hearthstead.guide.items.goods.tip: Better workers make better goods, and better goods sell for more.
hearthstead.guide.items.fish_game.title: Fish and game
hearthstead.guide.items.fish_game.b1: What your Fisher catches and your Hunter brings home.
hearthstead.guide.items.fish_game.tip: Plain fish in the Banner become meals for everyone.
hearthstead.guide.items.oddities.title: Oddities
hearthstead.guide.items.oddities.b1: Goblin loot and the settler spawn egg.
hearthstead.guide.items.title: Items & Tools
hearthstead.guide.ui.no_recipe: Recipe not available in this world.
hearthstead.howto.handbook: Press %s while holding it to open its Handbook page
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p2.b4: The hire card names the jobs that suit a newcomer's two best attributes.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p3.title: Strength, Stamina, Wits, Dexterity
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p3.b1: Strength: harder melee hits, 4 more items per Courier trip, fewer axe hits per log.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p3.b2: Stamina: tires more slowly, 2 extra hearts, keeps up to 80% pace when exhausted.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p3.b3: Wits: faster growth, up to 25% more trade XP and faster research.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p3.b4: Dexterity: tighter arrows, quicker swings, bigger fields, better catches and crafted goods.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p3.tip: These are the effects at 99; a settler grows toward them over weeks.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p4.title: Spirit, Perception, Focus, Presence
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p4.b1: Spirit: loses less morale, and Healers heal more.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p4.b2: Perception: Hunters search wider, Archers shoot farther, harvests sometimes give 1 extra item.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p4.b3: Focus: faster workbench batches, faster bow draws and spell casts.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p4.b4: Presence: better persuasion in talks, more Coins for Traders, happier Tavern guests.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p4.tip: Your best speaker (Trader, Innkeeper or Guard) handles persuasion.
hearthstead.guide.ui.caption.parley_talk: A raid captain comes to talk
hearthstead.guide.start_here.welcome.b1: You raise a Banner, give settlers jobs and defend them from raids.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.welcome.b2: Settlers do real work with real items: tools, chests and bags.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.welcome.b3: This chapter walks you through your first ten minutes, one step per page.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.welcome.b4: You start with this book; the Guildmaster by your Banner gives iron tools and 16 bread. Use Back and Next, or pick a chapter.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.welcome.tip: Press Next to begin. The Journey at your Banner always shows the same next step.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.banner.b1: Craft a Banner from 3 logs, 5 cobblestone and a campfire.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.banner.b2: Place it on open ground, away from other settlements, with two free blocks above it.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.banner.b3: Four founding workers walk in and rest by the Banner; the Guildmaster sits down beside it.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.banner.tip: Pick a flat spot with trees nearby: your first worker will be a Lumberer.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.journey.b1: Right-click the Banner to open it.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.journey.b2: Press Journey in the left rail.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.journey.b3: The Journey always shows your current goal and exactly what it needs.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.journey.tip: Stuck? Open Journey first, then this book for the how.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.lumber_camp: Open the Banner, choose Tech Tree and learn Lumber Camp.
It costs 1 Coin, 8 logs and 8 cobblestone.
Learning it gives you the Lumber Camp plan and the Lumberer Emblem.
Hover a node in the Tech Tree to see its exact cost.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.plaque.titl: 5. Build the camp and hang its Plaque
hearthstead.guide.start_here.plaque.b1: Build a small room: crafting table, chest, door, a light and 16 floor blocks.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.plaque.b2: Craft a Plaque (5 copper, 1 iron, 3 planks) and hang it inside.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.plaque.b3: Use the Lumber Camp plan on the Plaque, then right-click it for the checklist.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.plaque.b4: The Plaque glows green when the room is complete.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.plaque.tip: Fix one red line at a time; the Plaque re-checks the room by itself.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.hire.title: 6. Hire your Lumberer
hearthstead.guide.start_here.hire.b1: Buy a Lumberer Emblem from the Guildmaster: 1 Coin and 2 flint.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.hire.b2: Hold it and right-click a founder without sneaking: they take the job.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.hire.b3: Empty both hands and Shift-right-click them to see their inventory.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.hire.tip: There is no Hire button: the Emblem in your hand is the contract.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.zone.title: 7. Mark the trees
hearthstead.guide.start_here.zone.captio: Confirm the zone before it counts
hearthstead.guide.start_here.zone.b1: Craft a Work Scepter: 2 flint, 1 copper ingot and 2 sticks.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.zone.b2: Right-click the camp's Plaque with it, then two ground corners around trees.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.zone.b3: Right-click once more at the height you want, then press Confirm Zone.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.zone.tip: Include a few whole trees, trunk and leaves, inside the box.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.axe.title: 8. Give them an axe
hearthstead.guide.start_here.axe.b1: The Lumberer asks for an axe. Any axe works, even a wooden one.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.axe.b2: Put it in their inventory or in the Lumber Camp chest.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.axe.b3: They fell a tree in the zone and store the logs in the camp chest.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.axe.tip: Watch the first tree fall, then check Journey for the next goal.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.next.title: What comes next
hearthstead.guide.start_here.next.b1: Warehouse and Courier: goods start moving by themselves (see Logistics).
hearthstead.guide.start_here.next.b2: Farm, Homes and a Tavern: food, beds and new settlers.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.next.b3: Prepare for the first raid: it comes after about three days by default, even before you hire guards.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.next.b4: Journey shows each next step; this book explains how to do it.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.next.tip: Open Journey now and read your next goal.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.title: Start here
hearthstead.guide.founding.p1.title: Found your settlement
hearthstead.guide.founding.p1.b1: Craft a Banner from 3 logs, 5 cobblestone and a campfire.
hearthstead.guide.founding.p1.b2: Place it on open ground away from other settlements, with two free blocks above.
hearthstead.guide.founding.p1.b3: Four founders arrive and the Guildmaster sits by the Banner; later recruits each need a free bed.
hearthstead.guide.founding.p1.b4: Purchases take Coins and goods from you, then the Banner, then Warehouse chests.
hearthstead.guide.founding.p1.tip: Right-click the Banner and press Journey: it always shows your next step.
hearthstead.guide.coins.p1.title: Earn your first Coins
hearthstead.guide.coins.p1.b1: The Guildmaster's welcome puts your first 4 Coins in the Banner; sell goods to the first Traveling Merchant for more.
hearthstead.guide.coins.p1.b2: The first merchant sets out soon after founding. Later visits need a player within 80 blocks of the Banner.
hearthstead.guide.coins.p1.b3: Basic logs, iron and fish sell 8 per Coin; crops sell 16 per Coin.
hearthstead.guide.coins.p1.b4: Repeat sales of the same goods cost 25% more, so bring a mix.
hearthstead.guide.coins.p1.tip: Keep the Guildmaster's 4 welcome Coins for research and emblems. Sell surplus goods to earn more.
hearthstead.guide.coins.p2.title: Spending Coins
hearthstead.guide.coins.p2.b1: Spend Coins on Tech Tree knowledge, upgrades, Job Emblems and recruits.
hearthstead.guide.coins.p2.b2: Payments come from your inventory first, then the Banner, then Warehouse chests.
hearthstead.guide.coins.p2.b3: Winning the first raid pays 8 Coins; each later victory pays 4.
hearthstead.guide.coins.p2.b4: The Coins counter on the Banner screen adds what you carry to the Banner and warehouses; hover it to see both.
hearthstead.guide.coins.p2.tip: A refused purchase always lists exactly what is missing.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p1.title: Plaques make buildings
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p1.caption: A plaque's checklist
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p1.b1: Craft a Plaque from 5 copper, 1 iron and 3 planks and hang it inside the room.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p1.b2: Use a Build Plan on it to set what the building is.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p1.b3: Its glow shows progress: red missing, amber partly done, green complete.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p1.tip: Hang the plaque first, then build the room around its checklist.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p2.title: Read the checklist
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p2.b1: Right-click a plaque to see every requirement: space, furniture, storage, access.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p2.b2: Green checks are done; each missing line says what to build.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p2.b3: The room is re-checked by itself; Refresh checks it now.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p2.b4: Beds show their status on the sheet: yellow = free, green = taken, red = not in a valid room.
hearthstead.guide.plaque.p2.tip: Open Banner, then Buildings, to see every building's state at once.
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.p1.title: Learn new buildings
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.p1.b1: Open the Banner and choose Tech Tree.
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.p1.b2: Each node teaches building plans and unlocks Job Emblems.
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.p1.b3: Learn a node once its parent is learned and its quest is done.
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.p1.b4: Costs are Coins plus goods, all paid at once.
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.p1.tip: Start with Lumber Camp: 1 Coin, 8 logs, 8 cobblestone.
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.p2.title: Upgrades
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.p2.b1: Upgrades are one-time purchases in the same tree.
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.p2.b2: Early picks: Warm Homes, Sharpened Axes, Stout Straps and Guard Drill.
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.p2.b3: After the first raid, First Raid Aftermath opens the outer ring.
hearthstead.guide.tech_tree.p2.tip: Hover any node for its exact cost, requirement and effect.
hearthstead.guide.day.p1.title: The settlement's day
hearthstead.guide.day.p1.b1: Everyone shares one clock: Rise, Work, Meal, Evening and Rest.
hearthstead.guide.day.p1.b2: Workers walk to their trade in the morning and eat together at midday.
hearthstead.guide.day.p1.b3: A raid or real exhaustion overrides the schedule.
hearthstead.guide.day.p1.b4: Half of your Guards keep a night watch.
hearthstead.guide.day.p1.tip: Plan big jobs for the morning: evenings belong to the Tavern.
hearthstead.guide.research.p1.title: Research
hearthstead.guide.research.p1.b1: Research needs a registered Architect's Study.
hearthstead.guide.research.p1.b2: First finish the first-raid aftermath, then learn Commons Doctrine.
hearthstead.guide.research.p1.b3: Right-click the study's lectern to open the research bench.
hearthstead.guide.research.p1.b4: Hire a Scholar to push projects forward.
hearthstead.guide.research.p1.tip: Research is optional: build it once the first raid is behind you.
hearthstead.guide.research.p2.title: Projects
hearthstead.guide.research.p2.b1: Six projects are available; work on one at a time.
hearthstead.guide.research.p2.b2: Each costs paper and a trade sample, paid up front.
hearthstead.guide.research.p2.b3: Finished research gives a permanent bonus.
hearthstead.guide.research.p2.tip: Cancelling returns half the sample, never the paper.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.p1.title: Give a settler a job
hearthstead.guide.jobs.p1.b1: Learn and register the workplace, then buy its Job Emblem from the Guildmaster.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.p1.b2: Hold the Emblem and right-click a settler without sneaking to hire them.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.p1.b3: New workers start without tools; their need icon shows what to bring.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.p1.b4: Empty both hands and Shift-right-click a settler to open their inventory.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.stuck.title: When a settler gets stuck
hearthstead.guide.jobs.stuck.b1: Settlers who get stuck find their way back to the Banner.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.stuck.b2: Standing still for 10 s re-plans their route; after 20 s they step off an awkward spot.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.stuck.b3: Shut in for 90 s (fences, logs, a sealed nook): they are moved out with a poof and one chat line.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.stuck.b4: No block is ever broken or placed, and nothing they carry is lost.
hearthstead.guide.jobs.stuck.tip: Server owners tune this in hearthstead-server.toml, [pathing].
hearthstead.guide.jobs.p1.tip: A refused assignment never uses up the Emblem.
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.p1.title: Draw a Work Zone
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.p1.b1: Lumberers and Farmers only work inside a zone you draw.
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.p1.b2: Craft a Work Scepter: 2 flint, 1 copper ingot and 2 sticks.
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.p1.b3: Right-click the plaque or worker, then two ground corners, then the height.
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.p1.b4: Check the outlined box and press Confirm Zone.
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.p1.tip: A worker's settler sheet also has Edit Work Zone.
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.p2.title: What a zone needs
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.p2.b1: A Lumber Zone needs a natural tree with its trunk and leaves.
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.p2.b2: A Farm Zone needs farmland or a planted crop, with room above it.
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.p2.b3: Zones can be anywhere in loaded land, up to 48 x 64 x 48 blocks; keep them near storage so workers walk less.
hearthstead.guide.work_zones.p2.tip: NO WORK ZONE in Banner, Storage means that worker still needs one.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.p1.title: Couriers move everything
hearthstead.guide.logistics.p1.caption: Banner, Storage: stores and open requests
hearthstead.guide.logistics.p1.b1: Goods move for real: from workplace chests, in a Courier's bag, to the Warehouse.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.p1.b2: Plan about one Courier for every 10 settlers.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.p1.b3: Banner, Storage lists open requests; hover one for its route and Stop reason.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.p1.b4: Lay dirt paths or gravel: carts are fast on roads and slow on grass.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.tidy.title: Couriers tidy the Warehouse
hearthstead.guide.logistics.tidy.b1: With no delivery waiting, a Courier tidies: misplaced stock goes to the chest labelled for its group.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.tidy.b2: Half-full stacks merge into the same-group chest that already holds most of that item, freeing chests.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.tidy.b3: Rename a chest with an anvil, or lock it with the Work Scepter, and Couriers leave it alone.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.tidy.b4: A Warehouse employs 2 Couriers at level 1 and 4 from level 2; two never tidy the same chest at once.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.tidy.tip: Real deliveries come first: a Courier checks for them before every tidy load.
hearthstead.guide.logistics.p1.tip: Open Banner, Storage and hover the first request to see who carries it.
hearthstead.guide.crafting_orders.p1.b1: Workplaces open crafting orders by themselves when they run short.
hearthstead.guide.crafting_orders.p1.b2: An order checks the workplace, then the Warehouse, then a workshop that can make it.
hearthstead.guide.crafting_orders.p1.b3: If nobody can make it, it is marked Needs you in Banner, Storage.
hearthstead.guide.crafting_orders.p1.b4: Put the item in that workplace or a Warehouse chest and the order closes.
hearthstead.guide.crafting_orders.p1.tip: Check the top of the open requests for Needs you.
hearthstead.guide.summons.p1.title: Call a worker to their post
hearthstead.guide.summons.p1.b1: Right-click a working building's plaque and press Summon.
hearthstead.guide.summons.p1.b2: Its worker walks straight to their post, glowing through walls.
hearthstead.guide.summons.p1.b3: A summons lasts about a minute and a half.
hearthstead.guide.summons.p1.k2: Call the settler you look at
hearthstead.guide.summons.p1.tip: Lost a worker? Summon them and follow the glow.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p1.title: Eight attributes
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p1.b1: Every settler has eight attributes, shown on the sheet out of 100.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p1.b2: Newcomers arrive at 1 to 15 and grow only by doing the work.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p1.b3: Small numbers already count: 15 gives about 40% of the full effect.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p1.b4: Attributes make people different; they never pick the job for you.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p1.tip: Hover an attribute on the settler sheet to see what it affects right now.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p2.title: Attributes and jobs
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p2.b1: Each job has a primary attribute (green) and a secondary one (gold), shown first on the settler sheet.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p2.b2: A strong primary cuts work time by up to 10%, the secondary by up to 5%.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p2.b3: Wits makes every attribute grow up to 50% faster.
hearthstead.guide.attributes.p2.tip: Give each newcomer a job their hire card suggests.
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.p1.title: Trade levels
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.p1.b1: Each trade has a level from 1 to 10, earned by real work.
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.p1.b2: A steady worker earns about 25 XP a day; level 10 takes about 44 days.
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.p1.b3: Changing jobs starts the new trade at level 1 but keeps the old XP.
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.p1.tip: Keep a good worker in one trade to build their level.
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.p2.title: Which attribute helps
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.p2.b1: Each trade uses a primary and a secondary attribute.
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.p2.b2: Each level above 1 makes the worker up to 2% faster, at most 18%.
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.p2.b3: From level 5 the secondary attribute adds up to 8% more.
hearthstead.guide.trade_levels.p2.tip: Open More detail below for every trade's attributes.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.p1.title: Energy and Work Pace
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.p1.b1: Workers have Energy and a visible Work Pace, not a hidden quota.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.p1.b2: Tired workers keep working, only more slowly.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.p1.b3: The settler sheet shows Energy and the current pace.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.p1.tip: A slow worker is usually a tired one: check their Energy first.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.p2.title: Rest and Stamina
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.p2.b1: Rest and the daily routine restore Energy.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.p2.b2: Stamina decides how much pace a tired worker keeps.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.p2.b3: Missing tools and blocked routes are reported separately.
hearthstead.guide.dagsverk.p2.tip: Good beds and a Tavern evening keep the whole village moving.
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.p1.title: Recruit travelers
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.p1.b1: Travelers come once you have a valid Tavern, a free bed, good morale and food.
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.p1.b2: Before the first raid ends, the Banner needs at most 16 ready meals by default. Later, keep 8 per resident, including newcomers.
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.p1.b3: Open Banner, People, then Traveler and press Recruit Traveler.
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.p1.b4: A recruit costs 4 to 8 Coins, charged only if recruiting succeeds.
hearthstead.guide.recruiting.p1.tip: Build the spare bed before the traveler arrives.
hearthstead.guide.tavern.p1.title: Build a Tavern
hearthstead.guide.tavern.p1.b1: Learn Tavern & Inn in the Tech Tree.
hearthstead.guide.tavern.p1.b2: Build it with a bell, 2 chests or barrels, an Ale Tap, a door, 3 lights and 36 floor.
hearthstead.guide.tavern.p1.b3: You need a Tavern to recruit travelers and to be ready for the first raid.
hearthstead.guide.tavern.p1.b4: Hire an Innkeeper to brew ale and serve meals.
hearthstead.guide.tavern.p1.tip: Right-click the Tavern's plaque for its live checklist.
hearthstead.guide.tavern.p2.title: Tavern evenings
hearthstead.guide.tavern.p2.b1: In the evening, free residents walk to the Tavern and take a seat.
hearthstead.guide.tavern.p2.b2: A seat is a wooden chair facing a table, or a stair facing a fence with a pressure plate.
hearthstead.guide.tavern.p2.b3: One guest plays as the bard; eating while music plays gives +5 morale.
hearthstead.guide.tavern.p2.tip: Put three seats around a table so the bard has an audience.
hearthstead.guide.watch.p1.title: Arm your Guards
hearthstead.guide.watch.p1.b1: New Guards and Archers start without weapon or armour.
hearthstead.guide.watch.p1.b2: Put a weapon in Warehouse storage; a Courier carries it to them.
hearthstead.guide.watch.p1.b3: Open Guard Orders on the settler sheet: Hold Here, Defend Banner or Patrol.
hearthstead.guide.watch.p1.b4: An Archer at a linked Watchtower can take a Tower Post. Archers on towers and walls shoot farther and truer.
hearthstead.guide.watch.p1.tip: Stock a sword, a bow and 8 arrows in the Warehouse before you hire.
hearthstead.guide.watch.p2.title: Ranks and the captain
hearthstead.guide.watch.p2.b1: Ranks are earned by patrols and real combat, never chosen.
hearthstead.guide.watch.p2.b2: Rank armour must exist in storage before it can be worn.
hearthstead.guide.watch.p2.b3: The highest-ranked living defender becomes your captain.
hearthstead.guide.watch.p2.b4: Guard Drill: at 07:00 the Guards just off the night watch spar in pairs by the Barracks, for Strength and XP.
hearthstead.guide.watch.p2.tip: Let the same Guards fight every raid so they rank up.
hearthstead.guide.threat.p1.title: Get ready for the first raid
hearthstead.guide.threat.p1.b1: The first raid arrives about three days after founding by default. A warning comes one dusk beforehand.
hearthstead.guide.threat.p1.b2: Without defenders, expect 2–3 weak bandits. Armed Guards and Archers increase the first band, up to six.
hearthstead.guide.threat.p1.b3: A Barracks is not required for the timer. Ready meals, weapons and a clear route help you defend the Banner.
hearthstead.guide.threat.p1.b4: The band retreats at dawn; a separate time limit also ends a stalled raid.
hearthstead.guide.threat.p1.tip: Check Readiness helps you prepare; an unfinished checklist does not stop the automatic raid timer.
hearthstead.guide.threat.p2.title: After the raid
hearthstead.guide.threat.p2.b1: Open Journey at the Banner to read the raid report.
hearthstead.guide.threat.p2.b2: Replace lost equipment and restock the Banner's food.
hearthstead.guide.threat.p2.b3: Learn First Raid Aftermath in the Tech Tree to open new upgrades.
hearthstead.guide.threat.p2.tip: Raids now return on a schedule: keep defenders supplied.
hearthstead.guide.raids.p1.title: Raids
hearthstead.guide.raids.p1.b1: The first raid has its own timer; later raids return on a schedule after it ends.
hearthstead.guide.raids.p1.b2: A warning comes one dusk before every raid.
hearthstead.guide.raids.p1.b3: After a win the next raid is two nights later; after a loss, three.
hearthstead.guide.raids.p1.b4: Each victory pays Coins into the Banner: 8 for the first, then 4.
hearthstead.guide.raids.p1.tip: The Banner screen shows the next raid night.
hearthstead.guide.raids.p2.title: The alarm bell
hearthstead.guide.raids.p2.b1: Any bell inside the settlement is an alarm bell, the Tavern's too.
hearthstead.guide.raids.p2.b2: Right-click it or shoot it with an arrow for two minutes of alarm.
hearthstead.guide.raids.p2.b3: Civilians run home; defenders without orders go to the bell.
hearthstead.guide.raids.p2.tip: Ring the bell the moment you see raiders.
hearthstead.guide.saga.p1.title: The Saga
hearthstead.guide.saga.p1.b1: Every raid captain who reaches your walls has a name.
hearthstead.guide.saga.p1.b2: A captain who gets away with loot earns a title, like the Grain-Thief.
hearthstead.guide.saga.p1.b3: Captains hold a grudge against the settler who hurt them most.
hearthstead.guide.saga.p1.tip: Check the raid report to see which captain you faced.

hearthstead.guide.watch.body: A newly assigned Guard starts without a weapon or armour. Their need icon opens a real equipment request: place a serviceable weapon in Warehouse storage and a Courier carries it through their bag to the Barracks and Guard. Open Guard Orders from the settler sheet to choose Hold Here, Defend Banner, a two-to-eight-point Patrol, or Clear. After Arm the Watch, an Archer assigned to a linked Watchtower can receive the separate Tower Post command. Neither defender can fight properly until the requested physical weapon arrives.
hearthstead.guide.watch.body2: Rank is earned through patrols and real combat, never selected. Each credited hostile kill grants combat XP once and plays the experience cue. Strength unlocks the Guard's later abilities; any rank armour must also exist in settlement storage before it can be worn, so promotion never conjures equipment. The highest-ranked living defender becomes the settlement's captain. Archers follow the same physical-equipment rule for bows and arrows, earn their own combat progress, and return to their persisted patrol or tower order after a fight.

hearthstead.development.upgrade.courier_: Logistics, outer ring, sack tier 1. After the First Raid Aftermath, pay 4 Coins once: every Courier's sack grows and carries 12 items per trip instead of 8 (+50%; 14 with Stout Straps). Heavier goods fit too. No goods created

hearthstead.development.upgrade.hand_car: Requires the Courier Satchel. The cart rolls 10% faster on roads and 15% slower on rough ground, and waits outside while the Courier carries the last steps indoors. Its load is the Courier's own bag, so nothing is ever lost or doubled
Post-raid upgrade - 8 Coins, 12 planks, 4 logs, 2 iron. Courier trip budget +200% of base (12 -> 28 with the Satchel). Faster on roads, slower off-road. Locked until the Courier Satchel is owned
hearthstead.development.upgrade.worker_p: After the First Raid Aftermath, pay 6 Coins once: Lumberers and Farmers carry the village's sack tier too, at least +50% (8 -> 12 items at base Strength), +100% with the Leather Pack and +150% with the Frame Pack. Fewer walks to storage, no goods created
Post-raid upgrade - 6 Coins, one time. Lumberer and Farmer trip budget follows the sack tier (at least +50%). Locked until the First Raid Aftermath is learned
hearthstead.development.upgrade.guard_ar: After the First Raid Aftermath, pay 8 Coins once: Veterans wear iron chest and legs, Sergeants wear full iron. Recruits and Spearmen are unchanged, and every piece must still be forged and stored in the Armoury, a Warehouse or the Banner
Post-raid upgrade - 8 Coins, one time. Guards from Veteran up are dressed one armour tier earlier. Armour is taken from stores, never created
hearthstead.development.upgrade.archer_l: After the First Raid Aftermath, pay 6 Coins once: Archers shoot 2 blocks farther (18 -> 20) and draw faster (1.0 s -> 0.8 s). Tower Post range and arrow damage are unchanged
Post-raid upgrade - 6 Coins, one time. Archer range +2 blocks, draw 20 -> 16 ticks. Locked until the First Raid Aftermath is learned

hearthstead.development.upgrade.sturdy_b: Commons & Household, ring 2. Requires Hospitality, Warm Homes and 3 settlers housed. Pay 4 Coins, 3 Wool and 12 Planks once: every settler with a claimed bed gains +2 morale

hearthstead.development.upgrade.feather_: Commons & Household, outer ring. Requires the First Raid Aftermath and Sturdy Beds. Pay 6 Coins, 8 Feathers and 4 Wool once: sleeping settlers regain 20% more energy

hearthstead.development.upgrade.sharpene: Craft & Trade, ring 1. Requires the Lumber Camp and 16 logs stored by Lumberers. Pay 2 Coins, 2 Iron Ingots and 8 Cobblestone once: Lumberers fell each tree 10% faster, and every 8 trees they whet the axe at the camp grindstone
Bonus - 2 Coins, 2 Iron Ingots, 8 Cobblestone, one time. Felling time -10%; whets the axe every 8 trees
hearthstead.development.upgrade.fishers_: Craft & Trade, ring 2. Requires Shore Provisions and 4 Courier deliveries. Pay 3 Coins, 8 String and 4 Logs once: every Fisher cast finishes 10% sooner, and the Fisher keeps a net (1 fish an hour, up to 4), hauled in at the start of work and whenever it is full
Bonus - 3 Coins, 8 String, 4 Logs, one time. Fishing cast time -10%; a net catches 1 fish an hour, up to 4
hearthstead.development.upgrade.stout_st: Logistics, ring 1. Requires Stores & Roads and 6 Courier deliveries. Pay 2 Coins, 4 Leather and 4 String once: every Courier carries 2 more items per trip (8 -> 10); the Satchel and Hand Cart stack on top. A Courier with room left also takes one more pickup within 16 blocks on the same trip
Bonus - 2 Coins, 4 Leather, 4 String, one time. Courier trip budget +2
hearthstead.development.upgrade.leather_: Logistics, outer ring, sack tier 2. Requires the Courier Satchel. Pay 6 Coins, 8 leather, 4 wool and 6 string once: Couriers carry +100% of the base load (8 -> 16 items) in a bigger pack, and Worker Packs follow
Post-raid upgrade - 6 Coins, 8 Leather, 4 Wool, 6 String. Sack tier 2: Courier trip budget 16 items (+100%)
hearthstead.development.upgrade.frame_pa: Logistics, outer ring, sack tier 3. Requires the Leather Pack. Pay 10 Coins, 12 leather, 8 string, 8 sticks and 2 iron once: Couriers carry +150% of the base load (8 -> 20 items) on a framed pack, and Worker Packs follow
Post-raid upgrade - 10 Coins, 12 Leather, 8 String, 8 Sticks, 2 Iron. Sack tier 3: Courier trip budget 20 items (+150%)
hearthstead.development.upgrade.paved_ro: Logistics, ring 1. Requires Stores & Roads and 8 Courier deliveries. Pay 4 Coins, 32 gravel and 16 cobblestone once: every settler walks 15% faster on road blocks (dirt path, gravel, cobblestone, bricks and stone bricks). Build roads between your Warehouse and workplaces
Bonus - 4 Coins, 32 Gravel, 16 Cobblestone, one time. +15% walking speed on roads for everyone
hearthstead.development.upgrade.swift_co: Logistics, outer ring. Requires Stout Straps, the First Raid Aftermath and 12 Courier deliveries. Pay 4 Coins, 6 leather and 4 string once: Couriers walk 10% faster everywhere
Bonus - 4 Coins, 6 Leather, 4 String, one time. Courier walking speed +10%
hearthstead.development.upgrade.warehous: Logistics, after the First Raid. Pay 5 Coins, 24 planks and 4 iron once: a Warehouse whose room meets the Level 3 checklist is recognised as Level 3 (64 containers managed)

hearthstead.development.upgrade.great_st: Logistics. Requires Warehouse Racks and 24 Courier deliveries. Pay 12 Coins, 32 stone bricks and 8 iron once: Warehouses can be recognised as Level 4 (128 containers managed)

hearthstead.development.upgrade.royal_st: Logistics. Requires the Great Storehouse and 64 Courier deliveries. Pay 24 Coins, 64 stone bricks, 16 iron and 4 gold once: Warehouses can be recognised as Level 5 (256 containers managed)
Unlock - 24 Coins, 64 Stone Bricks, 16 Iron Ingots, 4 Gold Ingots, one time. Warehouses can reach Level 5 (256 containers)
hearthstead.development.upgrade.guard_dr: Watch & Defense, ring 1. Requires First Watch and one weapon delivered to a Guard. journey.hearthstead.step.fj_010_found_he: Craft a Banner (3 logs, 5 cobblestone and a campfire) and place it on open ground with two free blocks above it. Four founding workers arrive together, and the Guildmaster sits down beside the Banner.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_020_open_jou: Right-click the Banner and press Journey on its Home page. The Journey always shows your next step.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_030_appoint_: The Guildmaster sits on his stool beside your Banner. He is not a settler: he needs no bed, food or job. Your first talk is his welcome: 4 Coins for the Banner, and iron tools and 16 bread for each player. After that, right-click him to open Professions & Emblems and buy Job Emblems. A Traveling Merchant also comes to the Banner: trade logs, iron or crops with it for more Coins.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_100_unlock_l: At the Banner, open Tech Tree and learn Lumber Camp: 1 Coin, 8 logs and 8 cobblestone. No Coins yet? Sell logs to the Traveling Merchant near the Banner.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_110_link_lum: Craft a Plaque (5 copper, 1 iron, 3 planks) and the Lumber Camp plan (paper, feather, any log). Hang the plaque inside a room with a crafting table, a chest, a door, a light and 16 floor blocks, then use the plan on it. Right-click the plaque for its checklist.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_120_staff_lu: Right-click the Guildmaster beside the Banner and buy a Lumberer Emblem (1 Coin, 2 flint). Hold it in your main hand, then right-click the settler you choose without sneaking.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_130_open_lum: Empty both hands and Shift-right-click the Lumberer to open their real inventory and requests.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_140_set_lumb: Craft a Work Scepter (2 flint, 1 copper ingot, 2 sticks). Right-click the Lumber Camp plaque or the Lumberer with it, then right-click two ground corners around natural trees and once more at the height. Press Confirm Zone.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_150_lumberer: Let the Lumberer assess the job. Their request shows which axes are accepted; any axe, even wooden, will do.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_160_give_lum: Put one axe into the Lumberer's inventory or the Lumber Camp chest.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_170_lumberer: Keep a valid natural tree inside the confirmed zone and let the equipped Lumberer complete the work.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_180_lumber_c: The Lumberer must place at least one log from that work action into the Lumber Camp's linked storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_200_unlock_w: In the Banner's Tech Tree, learn Stores & Roads: 2 Coins, 8 logs and 2 leather (from cows).
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_210_link_war: Craft the Warehouse plan (paper, feather, chest). Build a room with 4 chests or barrels, a door, 2 lights and 25 floor blocks, and link its plaque.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_220_staff_wa: Buy a Courier Emblem from the Guildmaster (2 Coins, 1 chest, 2 leather). Hold it in your main hand, then right-click a settler without sneaking.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_230_open_req: Open the Banner and select Storage. Under the stores it lists the open requests and deliveries; hover a row to see its route, assigned Courier and Stop reason.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_240_request_: Leave the real logs in Lumber Camp storage and wait for the Courier system to publish their camp-to-Warehouse pickup in the open requests on Banner → Storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_250_courier_: Wait for one Courier to reserve the request and its exact physical stacks.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_260_warehous: The Courier must pick up, carry and deposit the reserved logs into Warehouse storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_300_unlock_f: In the Tech Tree, learn Cultivated Ground for farming (2 Coins, 8 wheat seeds, 4 logs) or Shore Provisions for fishing (2 Coins, 4 logs, 2 string).
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_310_link_far: Build and link a Farmhouse (composter, chest, door, light, 16 floor blocks) or a Fishery (20 water, Fisher's Chair, Fish Rack, barrel, door, light).
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_320_staff_fa: Buy a Farmer Emblem (2 Coins, 8 seeds, 1 leather) or a Fisher Emblem (2 Coins, 2 string) from the Guildmaster and give it to a settler.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_330_set_farm: With the Work Scepter, mark a Farm Zone over farmland or planted crops, including the growing space above. For fishing, link a Fishery with water, a Fisher's Chair and a Fish Rack.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_340_farmer_r: Let the Farmer request a hoe or the Fisher request a Fisher's Rod.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_350_equip_fa: Deliver the requested physical hoe or Fisher's Rod.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_360_supply_f: The Farmer must plant a supplied seed, or the Fisher must catch fish and hang them on the rack.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_370_farmhous: The Farmer must store harvested crops, or the Fisher must hang a genuine catch on the rack.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_380_warehous: A Courier must collect the workplace output and physically deliver it to Warehouse storage.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_400_unlock_h: In the Tech Tree, learn Home (1 Coin, 12 logs, 8 cobblestone) for the House and Lodging plans.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_410_link_fir: Build and link a House (bed, door, light) or a Lodging (4 beds). Plan for six beds in all: one for each settler, with room for two travelers. A House holds at most 4 beds, so use two Houses or a Lodging.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_420_unlock_t: Once three settlers sleep in linked homes, learn Tavern & Inn in the Tech Tree: 4 Coins, 4 bread and 2 leather.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_430_link_tav: Build a Tavern: a bell (gold or copper), 2 chests or barrels, an Ale Tap, a door, 3 lights and 36 floor blocks. Right-click its plaque for the checklist.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_440_recruitm: Keep the Tavern valid, one free bed, good morale and the current food reserve at the Banner. Before the first raid ends the default reserve is capped at 16 ready meals; later it is 8 per resident, including the newcomer. A traveler then sets out for the Tavern.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_450_traveler: Keep the Tavern valid until the chosen traveler physically arrives and waits for a decision.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_460_admit_tr: Open the Banner, choose People, then Traveler. Check the card's price (4 to 8 Coins) and press Recruit Traveler.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_500_unlock_f: After a real Courier delivery, learn First Watch in the Tech Tree (4 Coins, 4 iron, 8 logs) for the Barracks plan and Guard Emblem. A founder or recruit may take the Guard post.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_510_link_bar: Build and link a Barracks: 2 beds, 2 chests or barrels, a door, 2 lights and 36 floor blocks.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_520_staff_ba: Buy a Guard Emblem from the Guildmaster (3 Coins, 2 iron, 1 leather). Hold it in your main hand, then right-click a settler without sneaking.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_530_guard_re: Let the Guard assess duty and publish the exact compatible physical weapon requirement.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_540_equip_gu: Put any sword into a Warehouse chest. A Courier carries it to the Guard; that delivery also unlocks Arm the Watch.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_550_set_guar: Empty both hands, Shift-right-click the armed Guard, open Guard Orders and choose Hold Here, Defend Banner or a Patrol.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_551_unlock_a: Once a Courier has delivered the Guard's weapon, learn Arm the Watch in the Tech Tree. It is free, and unlocks the Watchtower plan, the Archer Emblem and the Tower Post order.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_552_add_fift: Keep at least five beds in linked Houses or Lodgings. The next recruit needs a free bed when they join, so aim for six.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_553_second_r: Keep the Tavern, a free bed, morale, the current ready-meal reserve at the Banner and the joining Coins ready. Until this Watch recruit joins, each traveler arrives in four to eight minutes.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_554_second_t: Keep the exact linked Tavern valid until this Watch slot's natural traveler physically arrives and waits for your decision.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_555_admit_fi: Open the Banner, choose People, then Traveler, and recruit the waiting traveler. Your Guard and Archer must be two different settlers.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_556_link_wat: Craft the Watchtower plan (2 paper, feather, iron ingot, arrow, white banner). Build it with 4 ladders, a chest or barrel for arrows, a door, 4 lights and 9 floor blocks, and link its plaque.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_557_staff_wa: Buy an Archer Emblem from the Guildmaster (3 Coins, 4 arrows, 1 leather). Hold it in your main hand, then right-click a settler without sneaking. The Archer must be a different settler from the Guard.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_558_archer_r: Let the Archer assess the tower and publish the exact serviceable physical bow requirement in the request queue.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_559_equip_ar: Put a bow (3 string, 3 sticks) into Warehouse storage. A Courier carries it to the Archer.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_559a_supply_: Put at least 8 arrows in the Watchtower's chest. Then give the Tower Post order (next step), which checks the arrows.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_559b_set_tow: Empty both hands, Shift-right-click the armed Archer, open Guard Orders and choose Tower Post at this Watchtower.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_560_declare_: The readiness checklist helps prepare five workers, beds, food and armed defenders. Check Readiness lists what is missing. The first-raid timer can bring a small band before this checklist is complete; watch its advance warning.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_600_receive_: The attack is set for a later night, never the one you declare on. One dusk before, a warning names the night, captain, direction and objective. Keep meals at the Banner and your defenders supplied.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_610_first_ra: Defend until the raid ends. Right-click any bell to send civilians to shelter; the Tavern's bell works too. Guards and Archers hold their orders. A victory pays 8 Coins into the Banner's stores. Raiders still standing at dawn flee, and a raid that ends that way pays nothing.
journey.hearthstead.step.fj_620_review_a: Open Journey at the Banner to read the raid report. Then learn First Raid Aftermath in the Tech Tree to open upgrades and doctrines. Raids now return: 2 nights after a win, 3 after a loss.

hearthstead.guide.builder.title: Your Builder
hearthstead.guide.builder.hut.title: Start with a Builder

hearthstead.guide.builder.hut.b3: Check the preview and material cost, then confirm the site.

hearthstead.guide.builder.sites.b2: Need is the unfinished bill. Hut/bag is ready stock; Warehouse still needs delivery. On way is cargo a Courier has picked up.

hearthstead.guide.builder.designs.title: Designs and defences
hearthstead.guide.builder.designs.tip: The Builder works from your orders; you can still build by hand.
hearthstead.guide.builder.designs.b1: Use the Survey Rod on two corners of your own build and save it under Our Designs.
hearthstead.guide.builder.designs.b2: Choose a defence line in the Builder's Plan to order walls or barricades.
hearthstead.guide.builder.designs.b3: Check the footprint before confirming work near buildings you want to keep.
hearthstead.guide.builder.upgrades.title: Upgrade a room
hearthstead.guide.builder.upgrades.tip: A room's contents determine its level.
hearthstead.guide.builder.upgrades.b1: Choose a registered building in the plan's Upgrade tab and read its missing checklist items.
hearthstead.guide.builder.upgrades.b2: Confirm an Upgrade Order for the changes the Builder can place.
hearthstead.guide.builder.upgrades.b3: Make any changes marked for hand work yourself, then check the plaque again.
hearthstead.guide.command.title: Command your defenders
hearthstead.guide.command.roles.title: Two keys: aim and tap
hearthstead.guide.command.roles.tip: Keep defenders within earshot (48 blocks) when you give an order.
hearthstead.guide.command.roles.b1: One key commands the melee troops (Knights, Spearmen, Longswordsmen, Healers), the other the ranged (Archers, Rune Mages).
hearthstead.guide.command.roles.b2: Tap it at a raider: they attack it, and when it falls they keep attacking the next raider until you give another order.
hearthstead.guide.command.roles.b3: Tap at the ground: they form a line there, facing your view. At a wall, ranged troops climb it; melee hold its foot.
hearthstead.guide.command.roles.b4: Tap it at a settler to summon that settler to you. Every binding can be changed in Controls.
hearthstead.guide.command.recall.title: Hold for more orders
hearthstead.guide.command.recall.tip: A sleeping, fleeing or unreachable settler may be unable to answer Summon.
hearthstead.guide.command.recall.b1: Hold a command key for a moment to open that group's order strip, then press a number (or scroll and right-click).
hearthstead.guide.command.recall.b2: Melee: follow me (about five blocks away), back to posts. Ranged: hold fire, follow me, back to posts.
hearthstead.guide.command.recall.b3: Hold Sneak and tap a command key to send that group straight back to its posts.
hearthstead.guide.finisher_revive.title: Finishers and rescue
hearthstead.guide.finisher_revive.finish: Without a separate binding, Finish uses the melee command key.
Only an enemy that lost its balance (staggered, stunned, bashed or knocked back) AND is below 10% health can be finished.
Its torso glows red: get in reach, aim and press Finish before it steadies (about 2 s) or heals.
Look at an enemy: its heart and HP show at the top of the screen, and turn gold when it can be finished.
hearthstead.guide.finisher_revive.rescue: Act before the downed timer runs out.
Approach a downed player and hold Use on them to revive them.
Use Sneak with Use to drag a downed player out of danger.
Keep the rescue area safe while your friend is getting back up.
Only players go down. Settlers who fall die for good; their job and bed free up.

hearthstead.guide.battle_roles.front.b2: Hire Spearmen at a Pike Yard to hold enemies at reach.
hearthstead.guide.battle_roles.front.b3: Hire Longswordsmen at a Sword Hall for heavy, two-handed attacks.

hearthstead.guide.battle_roles.support.b: Hire Archers at a Watchtower and stock bows and arrows.
Hire Rune Mages at a Rune Hall and keep rune stones available.
Hire Healers at an Infirmary and supply their healing materials.

hearthstead.guide.quality.grades.more:
The six grades are Basic, Fine, Superior, Exceptional, Masterwork and Legendary. For crafted goods, your worker's trade level matters most; their trade attribute, workshop level and tool also help. Masterwork requires at least trade level 7 and Legendary at least level 9, but neither is guaranteed. Better equipment can gain durability, weapon damage or armour toughness, and better food can give more saturation. Read the actual item tooltip for its bonuses.

With quality premiums enabled, crafted goods aim for 1.25 / 1.5 / 2 / 3 / 5 times the Basic price from Fine through Legendary. Offers round to whole items and Coins, with at most 5 Coins per sale. The merchant's shared purse still limits what you can sell: a valuable item cannot pay out Coins the visitor no longer has.

hearthstead.guide.housing_limits.beds.ti: Check the House plaque before adding more beds.
hearthstead.guide.housing_limits.beds.mo: Only beds in valid housing count. Extra House beds beyond the cap do not add new places. Existing residents are not evicted when the cap limits new claims. The village keeps a minimum of four founder places.

hearthstead.guide.housing_limits.beds.b2: Learn Townhouses to raise each House to six places, then Manors to raise it to eight.
hearthstead.guide.housing_limits.beds.b3: Add real beds: a higher cap does not create sleeping places.
hearthstead.guide.housing_limits.tiers.b: A House plaque names its home tier: Hut at level 1, Cottage at level 2, Townhouse at level 3 and Manor at level 4.
Each tier after the Hut also needs its node: Cottages, Townhouses, then Manors. Until then the House keeps the lower name.
Below the tier, the plaque shows the next home goal and what the next level needs. A Builder's Upgrade Order can add it.
hearthstead.guide.housing_limits.tiers.t: A Manor: 5 lights, 2 storage, solid floor, furnishing 6, a workbench, 25 floor space. With Manors: +2 morale.
hearthstead.guide.food_overflow.title: Warehouse food overflow
Make space for food before taking on more residents.

Food and crops can use other eligible chests in the same Warehouse when their normal storage has no room. Existing labels stay unchanged. This fallback still needs actual empty space; it does not create extra capacity. Personal stock and job-receipt stock are excluded.
Watch for the notice: Warehouse full, food overflow.
Add chests or upgrade the Warehouse when food has no suitable storage space.
Keep Warehouse routes open so Couriers can carry food to the Banner.
hearthstead.guide.visitor_departure.fare: Leave a clear road out of the village.

Departing event actors use the shared departure system. They try to walk out before being removed. Removal also checks every player: nobody may be within 24 blocks, and anyone within 48 blocks must lack line of sight. A stuck visitor can be removed after its timeout only when those visibility checks pass.
Let departing visitors walk away after their event ends.
Keep an exit route open for the departing group.
Give a stuck visitor room to find another route.
hearthstead.guide.attribute_effects.body: Match a worker to the primary and secondary attributes shown for the job.

Attributes support trade skill rather than replacing it. Wits also improves attribute growth. At default effect strength, the other bonuses grow with the square root of the attribute value: early gains matter, while later gains are smaller.
Use Strength for harder melee hits and larger carrying loads.
Use Stamina for more health and slower energy loss at work.
Use Dexterity for tighter arrow spread and faster recovery between melee swings.
Use Wits to support learning, trade experience and Scholar research.
hearthstead.guide.attribute_effects.mind: Check the settler sheet to see how a worker fits the job.

Perception can add an item to harvests, mining, shearing and fishing. Presence can improve conversation persuasion through the village's best speaker. Server settings affect bonus strength; work-time reductions have a combined cap.
Use Spirit to reduce morale loss and strengthen a Healer's healing.
Use Perception for longer searches, longer Archer range and chances of extra gathered items.
Use Focus for faster workshop batches, bow draws, rune casts and study.
Use Presence for persuasion, trading returns and stronger Innkeeper hospitality.
hearthstead.guide.hero_captain.title: Your hero Captain
hearthstead.guide.hero_captain.hero.b1: Learn Captain's Commission to field-promote your leading Guard to Sergeant.
hearthstead.guide.hero_captain.hero.b2: Give your Captain a name and choose a weapon loadout.
hearthstead.guide.hero_captain.hero.b3: Choose Sword and Shield, Dual Swords, Double Axe or Bow.
hearthstead.guide.hero_captain.hero.tip: Match your chosen loadout to the weapons you can supply.
hearthstead.guide.hero_captain.hero.more: Captain's Commission grants a one-time field promotion. If you have no Guard yet, promotion waits for one. With default settings, the hero gains 16 maximum health (24 to 40 before other bonuses), 4 armour, 2 attack damage and 0.5 knockback resistance. The Captain appears 13% larger while keeping the normal hitbox. Switching loadouts gives a 3-second re-arm delay before specials can fire; it does not reset their cooldowns. Halberd and Warhammer loadouts are hidden by default.
Choose Sword and Shield for Shield Charge, Hold the Line and Pommel Stun.
Choose Dual Swords for Blade Whirl, Twin Thrust, Disarm and Dodge Step.
Choose Double Axe for Cleave, Spinning Chop and Armour Breaker.
Choose Bow for Arrow Volley, Piercing Shot and Mark Target.
Keep a complete weapon kit equipped so your Captain can use its specials.

Your Captain chooses specials automatically as the fight changes. Every loadout shares Rally Cry, Second Wind and Execution. Second Wind heals 40% of maximum health when below 30%, once per fight; Execution targets enemies at or below 25% health. Specials have separate cooldowns and target authorized enemies, with friendly fire disabled. There are 22 specials across all six loadouts, including the two optional loadouts: Halberd adds Sweep, Brace vs Charge and Hook Pull; Warhammer adds Shield Breaker, Ground Slam and Crushing Blow. The four default loadouts share 16 distinct specials in total.

hearthstead.guide.weapons.title: Weapons
hearthstead.guide.weapons.materials.tip: Check durability as well as damage: golden weapons wear out quickly.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.materials.more: The five families are Short Sword, Longsword, Double Axe, Halberd and Warhammer. Material order in the following pages is wooden, stone, iron, golden, diamond, netherite. Durability in that order is 59, 131, 250, 32, 1561 and 2031. Damage figures are total base player attack damage before armour, enchantments, special traits and other bonuses; they are not Captain damage totals. Two damage points equal one heart. Attack speed describes recharge rate, not guaranteed damage per second.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.materials.b1: Choose from wooden, stone, iron, golden, diamond and netherite weapons.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.materials.b2: Craft the first five materials at a crafting table once any required technology is learned.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.materials.b3: Upgrade a diamond weapon at a smithing table with a Netherite Upgrade template and netherite ingot.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.short_sword.ti: Use the Captain loadout selector to choose Dual Swords.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.short_sword.mo: Base player damage by material: 3 / 4 / 5 / 3 / 6 / 7. Attack speed: 2.0 per second. Short swords support sword sweeping. Dual Swords Captain specials require the hero and a complete equipped loadout; carrying two swords as a player does not grant those hero specials.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.short_sword.b1: Choose a short sword for quick attacks.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.short_sword.b2: Equip a sword in each hand for the Captain's Dual Swords loadout.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.longsword.tip: Let the attack recharge before striking again.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.longsword.more: Base player damage by material: 5 / 6 / 7 / 5 / 8 / 9. Attack speed: 1.0 per second. Longswords are the battle-role weapon family; do not confuse them with the Short Swords used for the Captain's paired loadout.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.longsword.b1: Choose a longsword for slower, heavier attacks.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.longsword.b2: Supply the appropriate battle role with a longsword after unlocking it.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.double_axe.tip: Keep the Captain's offhand empty for this two-handed loadout.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.double_axe.mor: Base player damage by material: 8 / 9 / 10 / 8 / 11 / 12. Attack speed: 0.8 per second. With default weapon traits enabled, hits add 0.3 damage per target armour point, capped at 4, plus 2 against raid Brutes. This weapon trait adds damage; it does not permanently remove armour. The weapon can disable shields and supports sweeping. Captain Armour Breaker is a separate hero special.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.double_axe.b1: Choose a double axe against armoured foes and raid Brutes.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.double_axe.b2: Choose the Captain's Double Axe loadout to use its hero specials.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.halberd.title: Halberds
hearthstead.guide.weapons.halberd.tip: Use the extra reach to keep some distance from an approaching enemy.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.halberd.more: Base player damage by material: 6 / 7 / 8 / 6 / 9 / 10. Attack speed: 0.9 per second. Main-hand player entity reach increases by 1.5 blocks. With default weapon traits enabled, damage against a charging foe is multiplied by 1.35. The weapon supports sweeping. Player use is separate from the Captain's Halberd loadout, which is hidden by default.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.halberd.b1: Choose a halberd for extra player melee reach.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.halberd.b2: Strike a foe moving toward you to benefit from its anti-charge trait.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.warhammer.tip: Expect slower attacks and no sword sweep.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.warhammer.more: Base player damage by material: 7 / 8 / 9 / 7 / 10 / 11. Attack speed: 0.8 per second; main-hand attack knockback gains 1. With default weapon traits enabled, hits have a 25% chance to apply heavy slowness for 1 second; raiders also stagger. Player use is separate from the Captain's Warhammer loadout, which is hidden by default.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.warhammer.b1: Choose a warhammer for knockback and a chance to stun.
hearthstead.guide.weapons.warhammer.b2: Use its shield-disabling trait against shielded enemies.
hearthstead.guide.work_yards.title: Work yards
hearthstead.guide.work_yards.setup.title: An outdoor workplace
hearthstead.guide.work_yards.setup.b1: Enclose your work yard with fences or walls and provide a gate or door.
hearthstead.guide.work_yards.setup.b2: Cover at least four yard cells with a tool shelter.
hearthstead.guide.work_yards.setup.b3: Place the plaque facing into the yard, then meet its listed job requirements.
hearthstead.guide.work_yards.setup.tip: Keep a clear route through the gate to storage and workstations.
hearthstead.guide.work_yards.setup.more: These workplaces accept a yard or a complete enclosed room: Lumber Camp, Sawmill, Mine, Mason's Yard, Smithy, Smelter, Tannery, Builder's Hut, Well House and Market. Other building types still require their own room rules. Existing complete rooms are checked first. The yard survey spreads horizontally from the plaque side and requires a bounded area; opening a gate does not erase that boundary. The current limit is 512 yard cells, with the scan extending at most 24 blocks from its starting cell along either horizontal axis. At least four cells need cover two to five blocks above foot level. A yard still needs every workstation, storage container, entrance, light and minimum area shown on its plaque.

hearthstead.guide.taverns_ale.title: Taverns & ale
hearthstead.guide.taverns_ale.levels.b1: One ale makes a settler tipsy: a gentle sway without a movement slowdown.
hearthstead.guide.taverns_ale.levels.b2: A second ale before the first wears off makes them drunk: weaving, stumbles and slower movement.

hearthstead.guide.taverns_ale.levels.tip: Guards, Archers and other martial workers never get drunk.
hearthstead.guide.taverns_ale.levels.mor: Drunk settlers lose 25% of base movement speed; very drunk settlers lose 40%. Work takes longer at both levels. Panic, combat and raid alerts immediately suppress the movement effects, including weaving, stumbles and falls. They do not erase the remaining ale points.
hearthstead.guide.taverns_ale.recovery.b: Each ale adds one point, up to four. One point wears off every 2,400 game ticks.
At normal tick speed, one point takes two minutes to wear off. More ale extends recovery.
Remaining points survive saving and loading, with elapsed game time counted toward recovery.
hearthstead.guide.taverns_ale.recovery.t: The displayed level rounds remaining points up, with very drunk as the highest level.
hearthstead.guide.taverns_ale.recovery.m: This describes settlers drinking at the Tavern. A server can turn drunkenness off in the livingVillage settings. See Tavern Evenings for the building, staff, seating and service requirements.

hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.title: The Guildmaster
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p1.title: Professions & Emblems
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p1.b1: The Guildmaster sits on his stool beside your Banner. He appears when the Banner is raised.
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p1.b2: He is not a settler: he takes no bed, food, founder place or job.
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p1.b3: Right-click him to open Professions & Emblems: pick a profession on the left, check what it takes on the right.
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p1.b4: Choose a quantity and press Buy. Coins and goods come from your inventory, the Banner and linked Warehouses.
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p1.tip: He cannot be hurt and raiders ignore him. If the Banner is removed, he leaves with it.
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p2.title: Buying and using an emblem
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p2.b1: TO BUY: the profession must be learned in the Banner's Tech Tree, and you pay its price in Coins and goods.
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p2.b2: TO WORK: the settler needs a registered workplace of that trade, and some jobs request a tool from storage.
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p2.b3: Each emblem needs a free inventory slot; with no room the purchase is refused and nothing is charged.
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p2.b4: Hold the emblem in your main hand and right-click a settler to assign the role. It is only used up if the hire works.
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p2.k1: Give the emblem to a settler
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.p2.tip: A greyed-out Buy button always says why: not learned, not enough Coins or goods, or no free slot.
hearthstead.guide.guildmaster.body: The Guildmaster trades Job Emblems beside every settlement Banner. In older saves, the settler who used to lead the settlement is now an ordinary settler you can give any emblem to. Every price shown comes from the same catalogue the Guildmaster charges, and the screen keeps what you need to BUY an emblem (research and price) apart from what the job needs to WORK (workplace and tool). Your first talk with him is his welcome: after you raise your banner he puts 4 Coins in the Banner for the treasury (once per kingdom) and gives each player a set of iron tools and 16 bread (once per player). A player who joins later gets his tools and bread the first time he walks up to him or talks to him.
hearthstead.guide.start_here.guildmaster: Right-click the Guildmaster beside the Banner to open Professions & Emblems.
A Traveling Merchant walks up to the Banner soon after you found it.
