Chop 16 logs now: 8 to sell and 8 for the Lumber Camp.
conversation.hearthstead.story.hollins.g: "Good day! I'm Marta Hollin, from the farm over the ridge. We saw your smoke and thought: new neighbours!"
"Marta Hollin again, and the whole brood. We couldn't keep away."
"We weren't sure we'd be welcome, after last time. But neighbours try again."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hollins.m: "Last time there were %5$s of you by the fire. Now %4$s! You'll need more bread than ours."
"You've built since we came: %8$s buildings now, where we counted %9$s."
"Fewer faces than last time. I'm sorry for whatever it cost you."
"Much as we left it, and that's no bad thing. Steady is good."
"A village now, they tell me. The last time I came, %3$s was a hamlet with a banner."
"A town! When I was last here, %3$s was barely a village."
"A castle's charter. I remember when %3$s was a town of wooden roofs."
"A kingdom. I will tell my grandchildren I knew %3$s when it was small."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hollins.w: "We brought a basket, bread and eggs and seed for the spring. Good luck to %3$s, from all the Hollins."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hollins.f: "Look at all those roofs! Tam says it's starting to look like a proper village."
"A real house already. The first roof is the hardest one."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hollins.o: Thank the Hollins for the gift
Give them food for their table in return
hearthstead.story.hollins.arrive: The Hollin family from the farm over the ridge has come to %2$s with a basket.
hearthstead.story.hollins.outcome.thank: Marta Hollin hands over the basket: bread, eggs and seed. "Come and see us some time!"
hearthstead.story.hollins.outcome.give_b: The Hollins go home with full arms and big smiles. "Neighbours!"
hearthstead.story.hollins.outcome.refuse: Marta's smile fades. The Hollins take their basket back over the ridge.
conversation.hearthstead.story.pell_rook: "Pell Rook, herald. I carry a sealed letter from my lord to the leaders of %3$s."
"Pell Rook again, with another letter. My lord writes more often these days."
"My lord was not pleased with how his last letter was received. Still, he writes."
"You were %5$s souls when I last rode in. %4$s now, my lord will want to know."
"New buildings since my last ride: %8$s in all. I shall report it."
"Fewer of you than before. My lord's condolences, if you'll have them."
"Little has changed since my last visit. My lord values stability."
"When I last rode here, my lord wrote to a hamlet. Today he writes to a village."
"My lord last wrote to a village. This letter is addressed to a town."
"The seal on this letter is for a castle. My lord has noticed."
"A kingdom. My lord writes as to an equal now."
"My lord wishes %3$s good fortune in its new standing."
"He is fond of you. There are %12$s Coins with the letter, as a token."
"He sends his compliments, and %12$s Coins as a courtesy."
"I will be honest: the letter is cold. There is no gift with it."
Accept the letter
Send a warm reply with a gift of Coins
Tear the letter up in front of him
you answered his letter warmly
you tore up his letter
hearthstead.story.pell_rook.arrive: %1$s, herald of the neighbour lord, rides into %2$s with a sealed letter.
hearthstead.story.pell_rook.outcome.rece: Pell Rook bows and hands over the sealed letter.
hearthstead.story.pell_rook.outcome.repl: Pell Rook tucks your reply away with care. "My lord will be glad."
hearthstead.story.pell_rook.outcome.tear: Pell Rook watches the pieces fall, then rides off without a word.
conversation.hearthstead.story.odo.greet: "Odo Farthing, merchant of the long roads. I heard the peddlers speak well of %3$s."
"Odo Farthing, back again! Visit number %7$s, I keep count of my good customers."
"Odo again. We parted coolly last time, but trade forgives."
conversation.hearthstead.story.odo.memor: "%5$s customers when I last came, %4$s now. Business is growing!"
"%8$s buildings! You had %9$s when I was last here. Somebody's been busy."
"Quieter streets than last time. The road takes its toll on everyone."
"The same honest village I remember. That's rare these days."
"A village now, they tell me. The last time I came, %3$s was a hamlet with a banner."
"A town! When I was last here, %3$s was barely a village."
"A castle's charter. I remember when %3$s was a town of wooden roofs."
"A kingdom. I will tell my grandchildren I knew %3$s when it was small."
conversation.hearthstead.story.odo.wish: "Good luck to you, and good trade. I'll be back."
conversation.hearthstead.story.odo.fact_: "For a regular customer: a little something from my cart, free of charge."
"A first gift for a new customer. Remember my name when you trade!"
conversation.hearthstead.story.odo.opt.b: Buy Odo a drink for the road
hearthstead.story.odo.arrive: %1$s, the travelling merchant, has stopped his cart in %2$s.
hearthstead.story.odo.outcome.thank: Odo presses a gift into your hands. "Remember me to the peddlers!"
hearthstead.story.odo.outcome.buy_round: Odo laughs, drinks to your health and leaves a gift behind.
hearthstead.story.odo.outcome.brush_off: Odo raises an eyebrow and clicks his tongue at his mule.
conversation.hearthstead.story.wenna.gre: "Wenna Lark, songs for bread. I've made a new song about %3$s. Would you hear it?"
"Wenna Lark again. Visit number %7$s, and I've a song for every one."
"You hushed me last time. I've written a better verse, so hear me out."
conversation.hearthstead.story.wenna.mem: "More listeners than last time: %4$s now, where there were %5$s."
"The town has grown walls of stone and timber since my last song."
"Fewer voices in the chorus than before. I'll sing for the ones who are gone."
"The same brave village as in my last song."
"A village now, they tell me. The last time I came, %3$s was a hamlet with a banner."
"A town! When I was last here, %3$s was barely a village."
"A castle's charter. I remember when %3$s was a town of wooden roofs."
"A kingdom. I will tell my grandchildren I knew %3$s when it was small."
conversation.hearthstead.story.wenna.wis: "May your gates hold and your songs be long, %3$s."

hearthstead.story.wenna.outcome.tip: Wenna grins and sings the second verse twice. Spirits are high tonight.
hearthstead.story.wenna.outcome.hush: Wenna stops mid-verse, packs her lute and leaves without a word.
conversation.hearthstead.story.brisks.gr: "Aldo Brisk, and this is Nessa and our boy Wat. We've come a long way to find %3$s."
"It's the Brisks again. We hoped you might have room for us now."
"You turned us away before. Things were hard on the road. We'd ask one more time."
conversation.hearthstead.story.brisks.me: "You've grown, %4$s of you now. Surely there's room for three more?"
"We see new buildings. Maybe there's a bed for us now."
"Fewer of you than before. You could use more hands."
"A village now, they tell me. The last time I came, %3$s was a hamlet with a banner."
"A town! When I was last here, %3$s was barely a village."
"A castle's charter. I remember when %3$s was a town of wooden roofs."
"A kingdom. I will tell my grandchildren I knew %3$s when it was small."
conversation.hearthstead.story.brisks.wi: "Whatever you decide, good luck to you all."
conversation.hearthstead.story.brisks.fa: "On the road they say %3$s has beaten raiders %11$s times and stands."
"They say %3$s turned a refugee family away. We hoped the stories were wrong."
"They say %3$s is growing into something. We want to be part of it."
conversation.hearthstead.story.brisks.op: Give them food for the road
hearthstead.story.brisks.arrive: A family of newcomers, drawn by stories about %2$s, waits by the Banner.
hearthstead.story.brisks.outcome.feed: The Brisks thank you for the food and walk on down the road.
hearthstead.story.brisks.outcome.decline: Aldo Brisk nods slowly and leads his family back to the road.
conversation.hearthstead.story.anselm.gr: "Peace on this house. I am Brother Anselm, walking to the shrine. May I bless your Banner?"
"Brother Anselm, on my way back from the shrine. I prayed for %3$s there."
"You sent me away before, and yet I have prayed for you anyway."
conversation.hearthstead.story.anselm.me: "You were %5$s when I last passed; now %4$s. Heaven has been kind."
"New roofs since I last passed. %8$s buildings, God keep them all."
"Fewer of you than before. I will say their names at the shrine."
"A village now, they tell me. The last time I came, %3$s was a hamlet with a banner."
"A town! When I was last here, %3$s was barely a village."
"A castle's charter. I remember when %3$s was a town of wooden roofs."
"A kingdom. I will tell my grandchildren I knew %3$s when it was small."
conversation.hearthstead.story.anselm.wi: "Good luck to %3$s, and peace to everyone who sleeps under its roofs."
conversation.hearthstead.story.anselm.fa: "Your %10$s guards look tired. I will pray for their arms and their feet."
"You have few swords here, so I will pray the harder."
hearthstead.story.anselm.arrive: %1$s, a pilgrim, has stopped at %2$s on his way to the shrine.
hearthstead.story.anselm.outcome.blessin: Brother Anselm blesses the Banner. You feel lucky.
hearthstead.story.anselm.outcome.donate: Brother Anselm blesses the Banner twice. "The shrine thanks you."
hearthstead.story.anselm.outcome.send_aw: Brother Anselm bows and walks on, murmuring a prayer anyway.
conversation.hearthstead.story.gerd.gree: "Mother Gerd Wyllow. I heard there was fighting here, so I brought my herbs."
"Gerd again, bandages and all. You do keep me busy."
"You sent me away last time. Wounds don't care about pride, so here I am."
conversation.hearthstead.story.gerd.memo: "More patients than last time: %4$s mouths, %5$s before."
"You've built more since I came. Build a sickroom next, if you're wise."
"Fewer of you than last time. I'm sorry I came too late for some."
"A village now, they tell me. The last time I came, %3$s was a hamlet with a banner."
"A town! When I was last here, %3$s was barely a village."
"A castle's charter. I remember when %3$s was a town of wooden roofs."
"A kingdom. I will tell my grandchildren I knew %3$s when it was small."
conversation.hearthstead.story.gerd.wish: "Keep your cuts clean and your people close. Good luck."
conversation.hearthstead.story.gerd.fact: "Let me see the wounded. I'll leave %12$s healing draughts as well."
hearthstead.story.gerd.arrive: %1$s, a travelling healer, has come to %2$s with her herbs.
hearthstead.story.gerd.outcome.heal: Mother Gerd tends every wounded settler and leaves her healing draughts.
hearthstead.story.gerd.outcome.buy_potio: Mother Gerd tends the wounded and presses extra draughts into your hands.
hearthstead.story.gerd.outcome.send_away: Mother Gerd sniffs, shoulders her satchel and goes.
conversation.hearthstead.story.brannoc.g: "Sergeant Brannoc, retired. One eye left, and it still knows a guard post when it sees one."
"Brannoc again. Came to see if your guards remember what I told them."
"You dismissed me last time. An old soldier's used to that. Still, I came."
conversation.hearthstead.story.brannoc.m: "%5$s souls last time, %4$s now. More to defend. Good."
"More walls to walk since I was here. %8$s buildings to keep safe."
"Fewer of you. I know that silence. I'm sorry."
"A village now, they tell me. The last time I came, %3$s was a hamlet with a banner."
"A town! When I was last here, %3$s was barely a village."
"A castle's charter. I remember when %3$s was a town of wooden roofs."
"A kingdom. I will tell my grandchildren I knew %3$s when it was small."
conversation.hearthstead.story.brannoc.w: "Keep your guards fed and your gates shut. Good luck, %3$s."
conversation.hearthstead.story.brannoc.f: "%10$s guards. Not bad. Let me see how they hold a line."
"%10$s guards and %11$s raids held. They've seen blood. Let me look them over."
"One guard? Brave soul. Let me give them a few pointers."
"No guards at all? Then I'll show whoever holds a spear how to stand."
conversation.hearthstead.story.brannoc.o: Share a drink with the old soldier
hearthstead.story.brannoc.arrive: %1$s, an old soldier, has come to %2$s to look at your guards.
hearthstead.story.brannoc.outcome.inspec: Sergeant Brannoc walks the line, barks a few orders, and the guards stand straighter.
hearthstead.story.brannoc.outcome.drink: Brannoc tells war stories over a drink. The guards listen, wide-eyed.
hearthstead.story.brannoc.outcome.dismis: Brannoc grunts and limps off down the road.
conversation.hearthstead.story.hilde.gre: "Old Hilde. I collect stories, and I've heard %3$s has a good one."
"Hilde again. Your story has grown since my last visit."
"You hushed me last time. Old women have long memories, dearie."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hilde.mem: "When I last told your story, there were %5$s of you. Now it's %4$s."
"%8$s buildings now. The story needs a new chapter."
"Fewer of you. Every story has sad chapters."
"Your story is the same as I left it."
"A village now, they tell me. The last time I came, %3$s was a hamlet with a banner."
"A town! When I was last here, %3$s was barely a village."
"A castle's charter. I remember when %3$s was a town of wooden roofs."
"A kingdom. I will tell my grandchildren I knew %3$s when it was small."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hilde.wis: "May your story be a long one, %3$s."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hilde.fac: "%13$s days since the Banner went up, %11$s raids held, and %4$s souls. That's a tale."
"%13$s days since the Banner went up, and %4$s souls. Quiet days make good stories too."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hilde.opt: Tip her a couple of Coins
hearthstead.story.hilde.arrive: %1$s, a storyteller, has come to %2$s to tell its story.
hearthstead.story.hilde.outcome.listen: Old Hilde tells the story of the village. Everyone listens.
hearthstead.story.hilde.outcome.tip: Old Hilde tells the story twice, the second time with better dragons.
hearthstead.story.hilde.outcome.hush: Old Hilde purses her lips and hobbles away.
hearthstead.story.thanks.line.first_raid: %1$s: "Thank you, %2$s. I thought the raiders would take everything. You stood with us."
hearthstead.story.thanks.line.day10: %1$s: "Ten days since the Banner went up, %2$s. Thank you for giving us a home."
hearthstead.story.thanks.line.pop10: %1$s: "Ten of us now, %2$s! I remember when it was only the founders. Thank you."
hearthstead.story.thanks.line.town: %1$s: "A town, %2$s! I never thought I'd live in a town. Thank you."
conversation.hearthstead.story.sigrun.wa: "I speak for Varg Ironjaw of the Blackbriar band. These woods are his. You cannot stay here."
"Sigrun Crowvoice, again. Varg's patience has a bottom, and you are close to it."
conversation.hearthstead.story.sigrun.me: "You paid last time. Varg liked that. He'd like it again."
"You sent me away. Varg does not forget."
"You talked your way out last time. Words won't work twice."
conversation.hearthstead.story.sigrun.fa: "Your %10$s guards will not save you from the whole band."
"Your towers won't stop the Blackbriar band."
"One guard? Varg laughed when I told him."
"No walls. No guards. Just a banner and %4$s people."
conversation.hearthstead.story.sigrun.ul: "Pay %12$s Coins and he lets you be. Or pack up and go."
"%12$s Coins, now, or Varg comes himself with the next raid."
conversation.hearthstead.story.sigrun.op: "Look at our guards. Tell Varg to find softer prey."
"We have little worth taking. Tell Varg to leave us be."
hearthstead.story.sigrun.arrive1: %1$s, herald of %2$s, rides up to %3$s under a black banner.
hearthstead.story.sigrun.arrive2: %1$s is back, with two of %2$s's enforcers.
hearthstead.story.sigrun.outcome1.pay: Sigrun weighs the Coins and smiles. "Varg thanks you. For now."
hearthstead.story.sigrun.outcome1.talked: Sigrun narrows her eyes, then turns her horse. "I'll tell him. He won't like it."
hearthstead.story.sigrun.outcome1.talk_f: Sigrun laughs in your face. "I'll be back, with friends."
hearthstead.story.sigrun.outcome1.defy: Sigrun spits in the dirt. "I'll be back, with friends."
hearthstead.story.sigrun.outcome2.pay: Sigrun takes the Coins. "Varg is satisfied. You won't see us again."
hearthstead.story.sigrun.outcome2.defy: "So be it." Varg's enforcers draw their weapons!
hearthstead.story.sigrun.outcome2.talk_f: "So be it." Varg's enforcers draw their weapons!
hearthstead.story.varg.sworn: %1$s has sworn to lead the next raid on %2$s himself.
hearthstead.story.varg.beaten: %1$s is beaten. The Blackbriar band will not trouble %2$s again.
conversation.hearthstead.story.hamon.war: "Reeve Hamon Stark, bailiff to my lord. This land is his, and you have not paid his due. You cannot stay here without it."
"Hamon Stark again. The due is still unpaid."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hamon.mem: "You paid before, which my lord remembers."
"You defied me before. My lord's patience is at an end."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hamon.fac: "Your %10$s guards are no match for my lord's men-at-arms."
"A tower does not make you a lord."
"Not even a guard. You are squatters here."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hamon.ult: "%12$s Coins, or my men will take it from you."
conversation.hearthstead.story.hamon.opt: Send food to the lord to make amends
conversation.hearthstead.story.hamon.mem: you made amends with a gift of food
hearthstead.story.hamon.arrive1: %1$s, bailiff of %2$s, has come to %3$s with a ledger.
hearthstead.story.hamon.outcome1.pay_tax: Hamon Stark notes the payment in his ledger. "My lord is satisfied."
hearthstead.story.hamon.outcome1.make_am: Hamon Stark counts the sacks. "My lord will accept this. This time."
hearthstead.story.hamon.outcome1.defy: Hamon Stark closes his ledger. "I will return."
hearthstead.story.hamon.outcome2.pay_tax: Hamon Stark takes the tax. "Wise. My lord will not trouble you again."
hearthstead.story.hamon.outcome2.defy: "So be it." The men-at-arms draw their swords!
hearthstead.story.gorm.back.paid: %1$s: "You paid last time. Smart. Be smart again."
hearthstead.story.gorm.back.killed: %1$s: "You killed my brothers. I brought more."
hearthstead.story.gorm.back.talked: %1$s: "Last time you talked. Gorm is not in a talking mood."
hearthstead.story.gorm.back.took: %1$s: "Last time nobody came, so we took. Maybe again."
hearthstead.story.gorm.arrive: %1$s and his brutes approach the Banner. They look hungry.
hearthstead.story.gorm.arrive_more: %1$s is back with a bigger band. They look hungry, and angry.
hearthstead.story.chat.left_unmet: %1$s waited, but nobody came. They've gone on their way.
hearthstead.story.chat.threat_arrive: %1$s has come with a message from %2$s.
hearthstead.story.threat.cta1: Talk to %1$s. Answer, or it counts as defiance.
hearthstead.story.threat.cta2: Talk to %1$s. The enforcers hold while you talk; strike them and it is a fight.
hearthstead.story.killed: %1$s is dead. Word of it will travel the roads.
hearthstead.story.enforcers_retreat: %1$s's men fall back into the woods.
hearthstead.story.herald_killed: %1$s is cut down. Her men want blood!
hearthstead.guide.world_events.story.b1: Some visitors have names and come back: neighbours, a herald, a bard, a healer, an old soldier and more.
hearthstead.guide.world_events.story.b2: Each comes for a real reason (a new house, a held raid, a new rank) and remembers how your village looked.
hearthstead.guide.world_events.story.b3: Upset one and the chat says "<Name> will remember this." They really do: later visits and threats change.
hearthstead.guide.world_events.story.b4: Threats warn twice ("You cannot stay here", then "Last warning"). Defy Varg Ironjaw twice and he leads the next raid.
hearthstead.guide.world_events.story.tip: Paying, talking and fighting all work; each choice is remembered.
hearthstead.chat.trade.no_sale.merchant_: %1$s the Trader found no buyer: the merchant moved on before the deal was done.
hearthstead.chat.trade.no_sale.deal_fell: %1$s the Trader found no buyer: the merchant changed his offer.
hearthstead.chat.trade.no_sale.no_room: %1$s the Trader could not close the sale: his bag had no room for the Coins.
hearthstead.chat.trade.no_sale.nothing_w: %1$s the Trader found no buyer: the merchant only wants %2$s, and there is none to spare.

hearthstead.guide.watch.colours.title: Guards wear your colours
hearthstead.guide.watch.colours.b1: Guards and archers wear a surcoat in the Banner's field colour, trimmed in its first layer colour.
hearthstead.guide.watch.colours.b2: Raise a new design and every guard changes at once; new recruits dress the same.
hearthstead.guide.watch.colours.b3: Each guard keeps their own face, and the surcoat goes over whatever armour they wear.
hearthstead.guide.watch.colours.tip: Design the colours at the Banner: click its hanging banner (Heraldry).
hearthstead.howto.banner.s5: Click the hanging banner on its screen (Heraldry) to design it and name your kingdom.

hearthstead.heraldry.name.unfounded: The kingdom gets its name once the Banner has founded it
hearthstead.heraldry.name.too_short: "%s" is too short: use at least 3 characters
hearthstead.heraldry.name.too_long: "%s" is too long: use at most 24 characters
hearthstead.heraldry.name.wait: Wait a few seconds before renaming the kingdom again.

hearthstead.guide.builder.plans.title: Building Blueprints
hearthstead.guide.builder.plans.b1: Craft a blueprint for any building you have learned: paper, coal or charcoal, and the building's token item.
hearthstead.guide.builder.plans.b2: Right-click the blueprint: the Builder's five styles turn side by side with size and materials. Hover for the full list; click one.
hearthstead.guide.builder.plans.b3: The ghost appears where you looked and stays there. Walk around it; right-click the blueprint to reopen the panel.
hearthstead.guide.builder.plans.b4: Confirm checks the spot and shows the cost. When the Builder accepts the order, one blueprint is used up.
hearthstead.guide.builder.plans.tip: Panel keys: arrows move, PgUp/PgDn raise or lower, R turns, M mirrors, Enter confirms, Esc cancels.
hearthstead.guide.builder.plans.t1: Blueprint recipes (paper + coal or charcoal + token): House: any wooden door. Builder's Hut: crafting table. Lumber Camp: any log. Farmhouse: wheat seeds. Warehouse: chest. Well: bucket. Kitchen: bowl. Bakery: wheat. Dining Hall: bread. Tavern: barrel. Lodging: any bed. Market: apple. Trading Post: emerald.
hearthstead.guide.builder.plans.t2: Fishery: cod. Pasture: any wooden fence. Butcher: raw beef. Hunter's Lodge: arrow. Tannery: leather. Weaver: string. Carpenter: any wooden slab. Sawmill: stone axe. Mason: cobblestone. Mill: stone. Mine: stone pickaxe. Smelter: furnace.
hearthstead.guide.builder.plans.t3: Smithy: iron ingot. Armoury: shield. Fletcher: flint. Barracks: red wool. Sword Hall: stone sword. Pike Yard: stick. Infirmary: white wool. Brewery: glass bottle. Library: book. School: ink sac. Architect's Study: compass. Rune Hall: lapis lazuli.
hearthstead.guide.builder.plans.t4: Walls, gates, towers, upgrades and the site list stay in the Builder's Plan. Creative players keep their blueprint. (The plaque's Build Plan is a different item.)

conversation.hearthstead.gm_welcome.line: Welcome, %2$s, and long may the banner of %3$s fly!
The guild backs every new banner: %4$s Coins for your treasury, iron tools for the work ahead and bread for the road.
Ah, %2$s, a new pair of hands under the banner of %3$s.
The guild looks after everyone who works here. Take these iron tools and some bread for the work ahead.
Come back to me when you need emblems and roles.
conversation.hearthstead.gm_welcome.than: Thank you. We'll put them to work.
conversation.hearthstead.gm_welcome.repl: Go well. My stool is right here by the Banner.
conversation.hearthstead.gm_welcome.chat: The Guildmaster put %1$s Coins in the Banner of %2$s and gave you iron tools (pickaxe, axe, shovel and hoe) and %3$s bread.
The Guildmaster put %1$s Coins in the Banner of %2$s.
The Guildmaster gave you iron tools (pickaxe, axe, shovel and hoe) and %3$s bread.
hearthstead.guide.founding.welcome.title: The Guildmaster's welcome
hearthstead.guide.founding.welcome.b1: After you raise your banner, the Guildmaster welcomes you with 4 Coins for the treasury, placed in the Banner.
hearthstead.guide.founding.welcome.b2: Every player gets iron tools (pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe) and 16 bread. A full pack drops them at your feet.
hearthstead.guide.founding.welcome.b3: A friend who joins later gets his own tools and bread the first time he walks up to the Guildmaster or talks to him.
hearthstead.guide.founding.welcome.b4: The Coins come once per kingdom, tools and bread once per player; relogs and restarts never repeat them.
hearthstead.guide.founding.welcome.tip: Spend the first Coins in Banner → Tech Tree, then buy your first emblem from the Guildmaster.
